utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, may we have the appearances, please -- yeah, of course, I'm sorry. Can we -- could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And now may we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Alex Demirdjian with Lisa Biersay, the case manager Thomas Laugel, and our legal intern Agnes Bugaj for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Zivanovic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic and Christopher Gosnell. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You're comfortable as you are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And before I begin with my follow-up questions, may I just make a little correction to the transcript yesterday. At page 4174, line 24, I referred to a document in the report and I said that it was for the record Exhibit P101. I stand corrected, it is in fact P1004. So I'll just make that correction to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If you remember, we left off yesterday with a document of December 1991 which had listed Arkan and his unit as member of the -- well, as part of the 12th Corps of the JNA. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us how frequently were Arkan and his men used in combat with the army?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think among the new documents, I mean the documents that were obtained after July 2012, there is at least one combat order of the 1st Military District concerning combat operations by a unit of the 1st Military District together with members of Arkan's group, Arkan's group being subordinated to the JNA, in the area of Luzac, L-u-z-a-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, let's look at that document. I believe it is 65 ter 6019 at tab 553.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, as Mr. Theunens indicated, this is a document that is not in his report, it is one of the new documents. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So we see here that it's another document of the 12th Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir. I mentioned 1st Military District, but it should be 12th Corps. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No problems. The document is dated the 30th of October, and looking at the document it's an order. We see a reference to a map. Typically what kind of a document is this, having regard to the body of JNA documents that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, when you look at the doctrine there is a whole series of what are called combat documents, and combat documents basically consist of orders whereby there is a hierarchy from the top to the -- from the highest level to the lowest level you start with directives, then you have instructions, then you have orders and commands, and the lower you go, the more specific they become, but of course they are addressed to I would say another audience, the highest level is addressed to the highest command and the lowest level obviously to the lowest command level. And this is an order here from a corps, it's an order for combat operations and -- I mean, military documents have a standard layout. And in addition to orders, there is also reports, and when we talk about reports those concern mainly situation reports. I mean most of them are regular situation reports and similar documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, looking at the bottom of this page at item number 2, there is a reference to a Tactical Group Vihir and it lists a number of units here. Do you see to -- I mean on the fourth line, I believe, the Borovo Selo the OdTO, the Arkan, Luzac, and Novi Sad volunteer detachments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to take you to page 3 in the English version which is page 2 in the B/C/S version. And I would like to bring your attention to item number 9, which again makes reference to these detachments and indicates that the Novi Sad, Luzac, and Arkan volunteer detachments will attack from the line -- well, and it gives us an axis. And as you mentioned the village of Luzac. So is this another example of Arkan's volunteers deployed as part of the JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's actually being employed as under JNA command and control to conduct combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, returning to my question earlier, I was asking you how frequently based on the documentation that you have reviewed was Arkan's units used or employed as you would say. Do you actually see a distinction here? You used the term "employed."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just say employed because you said deployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem we faced and this is not just in this case but also when I worked on -- I mean, from the start, I start to work in OTP in the Milosevic case as well as in other cases where I believed that it was relevant to have documents concerning the operations conducted by the 12th Corps. Over the years, and I think the records exist in the OTP or must still exist in the OTP, I drafted several requests for assistance which were then obviously reviewed by the senior trial attorneys to be sent to the authorities of the republic of -- I mean at that stage it was still the FRY and subsequently Serbia, four documents concerning the operations of the 12th Corps or OG North or Tactical Group North in Baranja and Eastern Slavonia during fall 1991. And I mean we obtained very few documents. This one is basically the only one to my recollection that explicitly mentions the use of Arkan volunteers in combat operations. On the other hand, you have the famous Biorcevic video where the commander of the 12th Novi Sad Corps at the time praises the role of Arkan volunteers during combat, suggesting that it was a regular occurrence that they were used under JNA command when combat operations were conducted by units of the 12th Corps in Baranja and Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And could we go to the last page in both versions, please. Yes. Here we see on the last page that the document is signed -- it says Commander Srboljub Trajkovic. In the B/C/S the term uses "komandant." Now at the time I don't know if you are aware, was he in charge of the 12th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Colonel Trajkovic was to my recollection the Chief of Staff. But the Chief of Staff as is explained in SFRY armed forces doctrine is entitled to replace the commander when he's not available and he can sign orders in his name. He's the only one who can do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I apply to tender this document. It's one of the new ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1685. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, there are many other documents in your report which refers to Arkan's men and yesterday you mentioned also the support that he benefitted from members of the JNA, members of the Government of Serbia. Could you tell the Court, again based on the material that you've reviewed, for how long Arkan benefits from this support?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean depending on the nature of the support, basically he remains -- Arkan and his group, they remain in Eastern Slavonia, I mean Erdut, until, if I remember well, the course of 1997. And obviously during combat operations there is support in ammunition, weapons, there were -- I mean, even if he was involved in, I mean, "business dealings," there is reason to believe that there was also financial support. And as was highlighted earlier, I think there was an order from the 12th Corps we discussed -- we haven't discussed yet but I remember now, you could only move from Serbia into Baranja and Eastern Slavonia by using one of the three bridges over the Danube, the one in Batina, the one in Erdut, and the one in the south close to Ilok. And especially during the war but also afterwards, there was -- there were control posts from -- during the war the JNA and later on the police of the Republic of Serbia. So they would see that Arkan and/or his people would cross. And especially I remember documents and they are included in the report here where security organs of the 1st Military District state that Arkan and/or his volunteers are involved in looting. Well, the looted goods they were brought to Serbia and that had to happen via one of the three bridges. So it was noticeable and it was actually tolerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we have seen some documents yesterday with respect to that, and I would like you to look now at another document from the JNA which is 65 ter 1371. 1371. This is at tab 317. Yes. Now, we can see here that this is a document of the 1st Army on the 18th of November, 1992. Perhaps just a clarification here, is this an old term that's being used, 1st Army, or is this a different unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may well be because the document dates from November 1992 and to my recollection the VJ continued to use the definition of military district. So it's probably an old heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, looking at the title of this document -- and, in fact, I believe, that there's a stamp just below the header which has -- what is command of the 1st Military District --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- right? Okay. The title here is: "Indications re: The Establishment of the 'Serbian army' centre and re: Criminal activities." And this is an interview that seems to have been conducted with a civilian which seems to be a source here; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. In the -- in this initial paragraph the topic is being introduced and they're talking about the formation of a Serbian army. And next it's about large-scale criminal activity involving the leading man of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, the Government of the SBWS, members of UNPROFOR, and numerous criminals and smugglers. Now, first of all, with respect to the formation of the Serbian army, do you have any information as to what this is a reference to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically. I mean, when we look at the context, i.e., the Republic of Serbian Krajina, efforts are undertaken between May and November 1992 to transform the Territorial Defence which had earlier been transformed into the PJM. So to transform the PGM into a Serbian army, I mean the Serbian army of Krajina, the SVK, it may well be that person, the individual, refers to that or to something else. I cannot state from --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The acronym that you referred to now, is it PGM or PJM?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: J like Juliet. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And just very briefly, we'll see it later, but what does it stand for, the PJM?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were the special police units in the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. May I take you now to page 3 in both versions, I believe. Now, do you see on the first paragraph here there is a reference to criminal activities in SBWS taking big proportions and partly spread even on the territory of Yugoslavia, SRJ. There is a reference here to connections between those committing the crimes in SBWS and the leadership here of the MUP, the -- including Stanisic. Who do you think this is a reference to when the word Stanisic is mentioned here, name?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, when -- Your Honours, when seen in the context of other documents -- I mean, other documents on similar topics, this would be Jovica Stanisic of the Serbian -- who was the head of the Serbian state security at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Then they move on to the Government of the RSK and SBWS, here we see a reference to Goran Hadzic, Ilija Kojic, Zivanovic, Radulovic, Spanovic, Milanovic, this is followed by members of UNPROFOR, members of the VJ, et cetera. And the last sentence here says that they are smuggling and reselling fuel, food supplies, supplies sent as humanitarian aid, et cetera. Now, have you seen this type of information in any other document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. For what -- the smuggling of -- I mean, re-selling, for example, of humanitarian aid and food supplies that was coming from Serbia during fall 1991 is concerned, there are other reports of security organs of the 1st Military District that link Arkan to these kind of activities. I mean already I think more than a year ago, more than a year before this document, i.e., in fall 1991. And the issue of the smuggling of fuel -- I don't remember any specific document from the JNA or the VJ security organs, but it -- it was, if I can express myself that way, common knowledge that even during the war the oil fields in Djeletovci was being exploited and that oil was -- I mean raw oil was being exported to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do you have any documentation which would point to who was responsible for this exploitation?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Objection. This -- first of all, I'd like a reference into the report as to where this particular topic is discussed because I would say this is outside the scope of the report. And secondly, we're really getting into matters, Mr. President, and we know what the indictment says, we know this is 1992 we're talking about. I question whether these questions are relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm a bit surprised by the objection. This is about criminal activities going on the territory that the accused was responsible for during the period relevant to the indictment. It also mentions other members of institutions that he was related to, at least that is what is alleged in the indictment. So I believe that this is dead-on relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And the link to the report, Mr. Demirdjian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Do you have an answer for that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just a second, Your Honours. Well, yesterday we were at page 241, if I can just verify here. Yes. Yes, well that is where the document is mentioned, at page 241, with respect to the volunteer units, Arkan's units, and -- yes, it is mentioned -- the document is actually at footnote 736 and it's mentioned in other footnotes as well, at page 240/241 of the report, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, it's helpful to bring me to the pages of the report because I'm sometimes a bit lost with the amalgamated report because I consider my last report as my working base. But on the next page, 242, there is a footnote, there is a reference to a discussion of a group, the Slobodan -- I mean the group of Slobodan Medic, the Skorpions, that talks about the issue of the Djeletovci oil fields and it's footnote 743.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Well, I maintain the objection, Mr. President. I mean, what seems to be under discussion here is smuggling of oil, other contraband I presume, in 1992 and beyond. Now, how is that relevant to the charges in the indictment? And even assuming with this reference to names in this document that other members of the JCE are mentioned, how is this relevant to establishing the alleged common purpose alleged in the indictment? So we would say that this is irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may offer one more response on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The document goes to clearly the acts and conducts of the accused, and his conduct during that period of time for which he is charged for. And again, the issue is what was the focus of his activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: What's the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The 18th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: November 1992. And did I hear the witness say that there was -- that this was going on already a year before that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, not necessarily mentioning the same names, Your Honours, but there are documents referring to Arkan, that he's involved in such activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the -- if we return to page 3 again, please. I'm interested in the source that is being used here. You look at the paragraph after the one we looked at. The sentence beginning with: "We consider that information very interesting. It also confirms some of our previous information, but we have to keep in mind that Aleksandra," which is the name given on the first page, "has had contacts with Stanisic before and also that she tends to make unpredictable moves. And that is the reason why it has been decided to terminate contacts with her." Now, is this -- sources for the JNA of this kind, is this something that you have seen elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would prefer to give a more generic answer in a sense. I mean, in the methodology called intelligence cycle and when you look at the face of analysing the information, in that face or processing the information there is a step called evaluation, and in the evaluation step you look at, you assess the reliability of the source and the credibility of the information. And it's common knowledge that an unreliable source can still provide credible information and vice versa. A reliable source can also provide information of a limited credibility. What we see here just on the face of this one paragraph that there would be reason to have some doubts about the reliability of this source because of the motives she may have in order to disclose that information. However, the reference to -- I mean, the phrase "it also confirms some of her previous information," would add to the credibility of the information provided by that source. So a source of doubtful or low reliability can still provide information that is credible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on to another unit that you discussed in your report now, and I believe this is page 164 of your amalgamated report and the equivalent in B/C/S is page 199. I apologise, that's page 160 -- well, 165, actually, the next page. Here you deal with the group of Slobodan Medic, Skorpions, and the unit of Vasilije Mijovic, and if we move to page 167 this is where you dealt with the Red Berets, that's page 202 in B/C/S. Now, with respect to the Red Berets, you cite in your report a document which suggests that the unit was led by a man by the name of Zika Ivanovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the reference you have made here is to a certificate which we could display on the screen, it's 65 ter I believe 1179 at tab 667. This is a document cited in your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: But for some reason, Your Honours, I have it down as a new document. I'll have to verify this during the break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be old because I have cited it -- I mean, I cited it in the Stanisic and Simatovic report and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: For sure there -- maybe also in the Seselj report, I'm not sure but, I mean -- and when you look at the ERN it's an old ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It's an old ERN, yes. It may be that it was recently added to the list. I'll make some verifications during the break. Now, this document here we are looking at is a certificate issued on the 27th of June, 1992. And we see the header here says: "MUP Serbia Unit for Special Purposes." Have you seen this term used elsewhere, unit for special purposes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, this is the official name of the unit that was colloquially called the Red Berets. The problem with the name "Red Berets" is that there were several units who sometimes out of their own decision, I mean in Bosnia-Herzegovina or in certain parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina and in other parts, started to wear Red Berets, there was confusion, but the official name is indeed the unit for special purposes of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the document is signed by Zivojin Ivanovic. Is this the same person that you referred to in the -- yes, Zivojin Ivanovic, at page 167 of your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And, now he makes a reference here to an individual named Jovan Vejinovic, a member of the unit, who while performing a task, a checkup patrol in the area of Ilok-Bapska, it appears that one of them -- one of the members of this unit was killed and another one wounded and Vejinovic is heavily wounded himself. Now, this is a reference to operations in what appears to be 18th and 19th of December, 1991. Now, are you aware -- well, have you any information as to the presence of this unit in the area of Ilok and Bapska in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least this document would show that the unit or -- that the individual was there in a military capacity or paramilitary capacity at that moment in time. I have some doubts to refer to the Red Berets or the unit for special purposes because in my recollection it was established later. But the groups or the -- I mean, this is very clearly explained in the Stanisic/Simatovic report and some of the parts, relevant parts of that report are included in the amalgamated report. We see an evolution that some of these individuals are already operating in groups linked to the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia and only at a later stage the unit for special purposes is established and then they move to that group. We even see paramilitaries, I mean volunteers, who were part of Seselj's group who suddenly when they go to Bosnia-Herzegovina appear in groups that are actually linked to the ministry of the interior of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will not seek to tender the document at this stage. I will just verify during the break if it needs to -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like us to move now to another unit which is Seselj's men, and for this purpose I will take you to the special portion of your report at page 518, in the B/C/S version that is page 587. Now, here in your report you explain that already in March 1991 Seselj visits villages in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem to lend support to terrified Serbian people. Now, Seselj was, as we've seen earlier yesterday, was a president of the Serb Radical Party. In a nutshell, are you able to tell the Court what were the goals of the platform of this party?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, in a nutshell, the SRS, one of its goals was basically to - and I'm paraphrasing - re-establishing what was colloquially known as Greater Serbia, i.e., unification of all the territories where Serbs lived in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, on the next page, at page 519, you make a reference to an article from Velika Srbija. Can you tell us what is this magazine?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Velika Srbija, or Greater Serbia, is the official party magazine of the Serbian Radical Party, SRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we can take a look at this. It is at 65 ter 144, which is tab 46. Now, you've told us that this is the magazine of the Serb Radical Party. Could you tell us, first of all, how do you assess its content when reviewing it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, referring again to the -- I mean the aspect of source evaluation, this is an official magazine of a political party, whereby the editor is -- I mean, is Mr. Seselj, so he is responsible for the contents. When you look at the nature of the articles and the wording that is being used, one could say indeed that there is some propagandistic contents included. But again for the -- I have cited for a number -- in a number of sections I always look for corroboration with other sources, but I believe it was relevant to know when -- especially when they were talking about their own activities, I mean the Serbian Radical Party was talking about its own activities or the activities of its volunteers, that it was relevant to see how they were representing their own -- again, their own activities, in particular to also reflect the mind-set these volunteers and the party that sent the volunteers had in relation to their role in the conflict in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I think it's the fourth paragraph or third paragraph of this document which begins with: "The Chetnik volunteer detachment ...," and it says that it was established pursuant to a decision of the central homeland department, et cetera. And at the end of the sentence it says that it was dispatched to Western Srem on the 2nd of April, 1991. Now, this is what you make a reference to in your report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of this page in the English version, and I believe that in B/C/S it will be page 2, we see an interview with the leader of this Chetnik volunteer detachment by the name of Miladin Todosijevic. Now, here we see -- yes, at the bottom of page 1 there is a question put to him and -- yes, he's being asked here where and when he received his recognition. And he says this was one week before the battle of Borovo Selo, where I commanded the Chetnik volunteer detachment. Can you tell us what is this reference to the battle of Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battle of -- I mean, as they call it, the battle of Borovo Selo are the -- is the armed confrontation between Croatian policemen and local armed Serbs, including SRS volunteers, that occurred on the 2nd of May, 1992 -- excuse me, 1991 in Borovo Selo, and where a number of Croatian policemen were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we move to page 2 in the English version, we can remain on page 1 in the B/C/S version. There are various questions about when this unit arrived and where they were posted. And there's a question as to: How many people did you have in your volunteer detachment? And here it says: "At the time of the attack there were 14 of us, Vojislav Seselj's Chetniks, two members of the Jovic Dusan Silni unit, and six locals." Now, this is the same unit Dusan Silni that we heard about yesterday; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, and these are all party-affiliated volunteer units or paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. At the bottom of page 3 in the English version, we start seeing an interview with another member of the unit, Oliver Baret, and if we go to page 4, and that's page 3 in B/C/S, the member of the unit here describes the events at Borovo Selo and describes the number of casualties. He claims here that on their side according to the witnesses and my observations, the killed includes 12 Croats from the legal specials, whose casualty had to be reported, and 15 convicts or tramps without families whose disappearance was not reported. Do these numbers match other documents on the same topic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, to be honest, I wouldn't be able to say so because I haven't looked at any Croatian documents in relation to this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And if we move to page 6 of the interview, that's page 5 in B/C/S, we see another interview this time with another member of the unit called Zoran Milivojevic. Yes, at the bottom of the page we see his name and we can go straight to the next page in the English version at the top of page 7. He states here that on May the 1st, so this is the day before the Borovo Selo incident, around 2.00 a.m.: We captured two specials, close associates of Branimir Glavas. He mentions their names and mentions that they were captured. At the end of the sentence: "When we captured them, the Ustashas were trying to take down our Serbian flag." Are you familiar with this incident?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I mean, what happened is that on the -- Borovo Selo is one of these villages with a significant Serbian presence or even a Serbian majority at that time. And we have the various events in Croatia where there is on the one hand Croats striving for more autonomy or even independence or secession from SFRY and on the other hand Serbs who want to stay in the SFRY and -- I mean, all sides create their own armed structures. And there's also efforts undertaken to remove people from another ethnicity from the territory one controls. Borovo Selo is a village in Croatia and -- I mean, the Croats had -- the Serbs had some difficulties -- or some Serbs had difficulties with the Croatian flag. So instead of having the official Croatian flag, they hoist a -- what appears to be a Serbian flag on an official building. So the Croatian police is sent to remove the flag from Osijek -- I mean, they are sent from Osijek. Two guys -- two members, sorry, are arrested or kidnapped, I mean depending on which side you stand and how you define it. And a day after a more significant group or unit of the Croatian police is sent to free the captured or the kidnapped or the arrested colleagues. And then we have this armed confrontation between Croatian police and Serb volunteers/paramilitaries consisting of Seselj's volunteers, members of Dusan Silni, as well as armed local Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You mentioned this incident also at page 439 of your report, which is the Mrksic portion of your report. In a nutshell could you tell the Court how significant was this incident?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the -- the most significant armed confrontation so far in Croatia so -- and especially in Eastern Slavonia -- I mean in eastern Croatia. It resulted in a serious increase in the overall tension and further polarisation creating the situation that we would witness then later on in summer and fall 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, having regard to what you told us earlier yesterday about the mission of the JNA, could you tell us based on what you reviewed how the JNA reacted to this incident?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, among the new documents there are a number of orders and situation reports of units belonging to the 12th Corps and the 12th Corps to deploy JNA units in Borovo Selo and other parts of Eastern Slavonia where the tension has increased in order to interpose itself between the armed Croats and -- between Croatian police and armed Croats and armed Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would ask that we display 65 ter 6013 at tab 549. It is one of the new documents that Mr. Theunens is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We see here that this is a document of the 8th of October, 1991, in the village of Dalj issued by the 12th Corps. And it is a report on the situation in the units. Now, first of all, do you see here at the third paragraph which starts with: "The 12th pmbr and the 51st Mechanised Brigade have been conducting operations since the beginning of the armed conflict ..." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. The second sentence indicates here that some of these mechanised brigades or battalions have been participating in the armed conflict since 4 May. And when they were sent to Vukovar and Vinkovci garrisons. Now, is this what you were referring to a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it's one example. I mean, there are several documents. This is a bit -- I wouldn't say unusual, but it's a kind of a situation report that covers several months because it states the 8th of October and it talks already about events occurring in May, but there's also reports, daily situation reports that talk about similar developments, for example, in Dalj and other towns in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, do you see the next paragraph, it begins with: "The 18th Infantry Motorised Brigade ... positioned in the zone since the 20th of September 1991 ..." The second sentence here says: "We have been securing the bridges on the river Danube in the sectors of Backa Palanka, Bogojevo, and Bezdan since early May 1991." Do you know what this refers to exactly?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's what I mentioned earlier. When you look at the map, there is no physical connection between Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem on the one hand and Serbia on the other hand. I mean, there is the Danube in between and there are three bridges. The locations mentioned here: Backa Palanka I mentioned earlier, it's the most southern bridge; Bogojevo is the location in Serbia opposite to Erdut, so it's what I would call the central bridge; and Bezdan is the most northern bridge is opposite to -- is what is called Batina, Batina Bridge, I mean it's opposite to Batina, and it shows that the JNA is controlling these bridges since May 1991. And later on, I mean in the course of 1992, there was still -- this is not in the report but I was there a few times and also from my work in UNCRO -- UNPROFOR, sorry, there was a JNA presence along the river-banks as well as Serbian police check-points on the bridges on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go to the last page of this document, the document here is signed by Major-General Miladin Bratic, so this was at the time the commander of the 12th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Bratic is killed in action early November 1991 and then he's replaced by Major-General Andrija Biorcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is one of the new documents. May I apply to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1686. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Returning to your report. At page 440 you make a reference to other groups of volunteers who arrived later that summer and you make a reference here to I think it is at item 4, page 440, to a detachment commanded by Branislav Gavrilovic, aka Brne. And this document that you cite to in your report indicates that he was deployed in the region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem between the 4th of June and the 2nd of December, 1991. First of all, have you seen other documents with respect to Branislav Gavrilovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the context of Eastern Slavonia or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Generally, meaning the conflict.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this -- probably not in this report but in the report on the role of Seselj volunteers he was also very active in northern Bosnia-Herzegovina during the take-over operations there of spring 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And in the conflict in SBWS you mention other SRS units, and for this I believe we have to flip to page 198. This would be, I suspect, part of your Karadzic report. Yes. In fact, it's page 199. That's in B/C/S page 238. And here you make mention of the Seseljevci volunteers detachment, the Leva Supoderica. In fact, at the top of the page you also mention the Petrova Gora. Can you tell us a little bit about these two units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These units are two local Serb TO detachments in Vukovar -- I mean, the names refer to neighbourhoods in Vukovar. And -- I mean, Leva Supoderica is also often identified mainly in SRS documentation but I think also in some OG south documents as a Chetnik detachment or Seselj volunteer detachment. And so in -- within these local Serb TO detachments there are indeed a substantial number of SRS volunteers predominantly -- I mean, particularly in Leva Supoderica, and Leva Supoderica, for example, was led by Milan Lancuzanin, Kameni, who, if I'm not mistaken, is also proclaimed Chetnik Vojvoda by Vojislav Seselj in recognition of his activities in Vukovar prior to the fall of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned yesterday that some of these units, when they were deployed in the field, they were -- there was a process of legalisation. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, yesterday I spoke about decisions that have -- that were adopted between summer 1991 and winter 1991 on the level of the Republic of Serbia in August. Then in September there is a similar decision or instruction on the level of the SSNO. And on -- in December there is the -- on the 10th of the December there is the presidential order number 73 to regularise, but in fact legalise, the status of these party-affiliated volunteer groups -- not only their existence, but also their participation in combat operations -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, could we look at 65 ter 443, please. This is at tab 122. Very well. We see the document on the screen here. On the top of the page, on the top left-hand corner, we see what appears to be -- yes, a stamp of the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, Vukovar, must be the municipal staff here. And on the right-hand side we see the date. Sid, 18 October 1991. Is there anything in particular you can say in relation to the fact that this document seems to have been drafted in Sid?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as long as combat operations were ongoing in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem, on the one hand we see efforts by local Serbs to establish local bodies of authority, also efforts to establish local -- or their own armed structures, obviously using the name "TO." And as long as they cannot operate from Eastern Slavonia, they maintain a presence in, for example, in Sid. And even later on there is a presence maintained in Sid. But I have no information as to when they moved from Sid, for example, to Erdut or to Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, with respect to the title "legalisation of the functioning of the unit 'Leva Supoderica' detachment," it indicates here that the commander of unit as you mentioned earlier was Milan Lancuzanin. Are you familiar also with the name of the person who signs the document, Dusan Filipovic? Have you seen this document elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously I've seen the document because it's included in my report. But at this stage I don't recall seeing additional documents signed by this person, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And again the term "legalisation" refers here to -- it's used by the drafter, whereby the drafter is connected to the municipal TO staff in Vukovar, which is at that stage not under Serbian control. It's different from the three kind of high-level documents I referred to earlier issued by Republic of Serbia, the SSNO, and in December by the Presidency, SFRY Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in relation to Milan Lancuzanin you explain at page 532/533 of your report, this is in the Seselj portion of your report, that he was proposed from a promotion -- for a promotion in December 1991. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we could display 65 ter 771, please. This is at tab 225.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe just to clarify, this is promotion within the whole - how would I say? - structure and organisation of the SRS volunteers, whereby the SRS, as is explained elsewhere, establish a war staff and they basically also establish a military structure, so a party-affiliated military structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in respect to that, actually, we see on the top left-hand corner that the document -- at least the header says "Territorial Defence municipal staff of Vukovar."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation as to why the header is used in this way if it's supposed to be an SRS document or --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't -- I don't think I said it's an SRS document, but it's a document that is sent by a person from the municipal TO staff Vukovar, so the local Serb or the SAO SBWS local Serb TO to the SRS because the SRS, as I mentioned, established starting in spring 1991 a paramilitary structure, referring to all traditions like the Chetniks they used military ranks but these ranks are not necessarily recognised by the JNA. And they have their own even rituals I would say. For example, people are proclaimed Chetnik Vojvoda, which again is a reference to history, but there is not necessarily -- this is not necessarily recognised within the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you see a name of Milan Lancuzanin here. Do you recognise any of the other names that are proposed for promotion on this request?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would recognise most of the names. I mean Miroljub Vujovic and Stanko Vujanovic, they also they were part of Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora TO detachments during the conflict and they participated with their volunteers in the operations to take control of Vukovar under the command of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And at page 538 of your report you indicate that these men, Lancuzanin, Vujovic, and Vujanovic were indicted by the Belgrade war crimes Chamber in 2003; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, and there was also a judgement in 2005, but I understand that judgement was quashed and I haven't been able to follow what happened afterwards, whether there has been a re-trial and if there was a re-trial what the outcome of the re-trial was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now -- and just to wrap-up on this issue, you say here that this was in relation the Ovcara case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. In relation to the issue of the deployment of Seselj's men, I would like you to look at another document which is at 65 ter 741 at tab 682. Yes. Here we see that it is a stenographic record of the Republic of Serbia Assembly. And it is held on numerous days during the month of December 1991. Now, in the English version I would like us to go to page 14 of the document. We're looking for the B/C/S equivalent right now because I don't have the correct page number. Yes. On page 14 at the bottom we see that during this Assembly session - so if we can scroll down to the bottom of this page in the English version - we see that Dr. Vojislav Seselj is given the floor and begins with a speech. I'm just waiting to see if we're capable of finding the B/C/S page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry about this delay, Your Honours. It would be at page 9 of the B/C/S version. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, on page 15, this is the very next page in the English version, we would have to move to the next page in the B/C/S version as well, we see Seselj saying here -- this would be the third paragraph which begins with: "As far as Chetnik units are concerned ..." And at the fifth line he says: "Where are these Chetnik units being formed? In those places where there is no regular government authority. We had Chetnik units in Eastern Slavonia and in the Serbian Krajina until the regular, legal, and legitimate governments of those countries were elected. The Chetniks were dominant in participating in the defence of Borovo Selo. When the government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was formed, we merged those Chetnik units with the Territorial Defence of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Today we have no Chetnik units anywhere ...," et cetera. Now, with respect to what you told us yesterday about the dispatching of volunteers and -- what can you say about Seselj's utterance here that they were merged with -- with units of the Territorial Defence, sorry?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not -- I'm not familiar with the formal merging process regulated by military documents stating when the process starts and ends and how it is conducted, but we see indeed -- I mean, Leva Supoderica is a good example where we have members of local Serb TO or local volunteers and SRS-affiliated volunteers who identify themselves as Chetniks who joined -- who start working together in one unit, Leva Supoderica, which according to SRS documentation is a Chetnik detachment, but in JNA documentation is referred to as a TO detachment. So there is, I would say, something more than collusion. There is obviously a -- you can call it a merging, but it's a -- I would call it more a de facto merging than a formal merging process.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we turn to page 169 of your report, so we're returning to your Karadzic segment, here you're dealing with decrees, instructions, and orders by the SFRY and Serbian authorities between August and December 1991. And here you begin your section with your conclusion that various decrees and orders were adopted between the period summer to winter 1991 to regularise the status of volunteers. One decree you refer to here is the 14th of August, 1991, decree, at the bottom of that page. And could you tell us a little bit about this decree, what it establishes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So these are the three decisions I mentioned earlier in my testimony. This one, 14th of August, 1991, is a decree by the Serbian government to register volunteers in the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia. The question could of course be raised why at that time when Serbia is not involved in, at least officially, is not involved in a war why volunteers would have to join the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I see. Now, this is the first order or decree in a string of two or three document -- three documents you referred to. I believe it is at page 172 where you deal with the decree on the registration of volunteers in the Territorial Defence --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- right? Okay. Now, generally speaking, having looked at these three documents, what is your conclusion with respect to the Serbian government's position with respect to volunteer formations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is discussed in the report, i.e., irrespective of this specific decree and the other decisions, i.e., the instruction by the SSNO of 13th of September and the order of the Presidency, SFRY Presidency of the 10th of December, so irrespective of those, the Serbian government takes measures to compensate party-affiliated and other volunteers for their participation in the conflict in Croatia, whether it is as part of the JNA, local Serb TO, TO units of the Republic of Serbia, or party-affiliated paramilitary/volunteer groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at page 178 of your report, that is 215 in the B/C/S version, you indicate at item 6 that by the time the armed conflict moves to Bosnia and Herzegovina in April or early May 1992, some of these units are still engaged, some of these volunteer formations were still active; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And we even see the same individuals. I mean, individuals move from one group to the other as I mentioned earlier. Individuals who were affiliated with the SRS, we see them appear in the spring 1992 in Bosnia-Herzegovina during take-over operations, whereby they are part of groups that are affiliated to the Ministry of Interior, Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, there is a reference here to a document that I want you to look at. It's 65 ter 1213 at tab 304, please. In fact, the reference is at page 180 of your report. Yes. This is a document drafted by the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, army Main Staff. Are you familiar with this document, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I am familiar with this document. I think when you go at the end you will see that it was signed by, at that time I think he was still colonel, Tolimir, who was the assistant commander for security and intelligence in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And what do we see in the first paragraph of this document? We see references to various units and what can you make out of the list of the names we see Arkan's men, Seseljevcis, Captain Dragans, Carli's, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are names of -- of the same names of groups we also see participating on the Serbian side during the conflict in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I would like now to move to the next segment of your report at page 181 onwards which deals with the Territorial Defence of the SAO Krajina and later the RSK. Now, at page 181/182, I believe you describe there some of the factual background relating to the creation of the Serb autonomous districts. And then you start talking about the TO. Perhaps - and this is I think at the top of page 182 - you indicate that the term TO is used here for those TO forces that are established by the Serbs in Croatia. And perhaps you could clarify for the -- do you need a moment, Mr. Theunens? You okay?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I'm okay. No worries.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps you could clarify for the Trial Chamber as to whether prior to these events in 1991, whether there was a Territorial Defence in existence on the territory of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. As we discussed yesterday, the TO, Territorial Defence, was organised on a republican basis, so each republic, each of the six republics and each autonomous province in the SFRY had its own TO, which was answerable to the president of the republic for its level of organisation, planning, equipment, and so on. And we see with the -- the events early 1991 in Croatia that -- I mean, parallel with the -- I would say the political process, that local Serbs start establishing their own structures. There are occasions where the Croats are removed or the Croatian -- or the Croats leave themselves. And the result is that with the assistance of the Republic of Serbia and in some cases JNA, local Serbs in parts of Croatia where they have a majority or a significant presence establish their own SAO TO which then later merges into the RSK TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, having regard to what you just told us that there was an existing Croatian TO, could you provide us with your comments about the creation of the Serb-only TO units in Croatia and the -- perhaps having regard to what you told us yesterday with respect to the doctrine and the existence of legally-framed TO units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I think -- I'm not sure I understand the question because the process as it occurs -- again, based on a review of the documents is described on page 182 and 183 -- okay, what I didn't mention but it goes by itself is that the local Serbs also adopt their own legislation; however, this is done with some delay. And as I mention on page 183, that is the Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia which was adopted in July 1991 and which was a bit, as I mentioned, controversial in relation to the fact that it mentions the term "armed forces of the republic," which was a novelty. So the SAO Krajina develops its own Law on Defence only on the 30th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is on page 183 --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: --- where you mention this. So --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And maybe I can add, but that's also in the report, that throughout this evolution the local Serbs regularly emphasized the unity between their TO or -- and even their police forces and the armed forces of the SFRY or what remains, actually, of the armed forces of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, looking at this law which is actually an admitted exhibit, P1248, it's at tab 67, if we can display that for a moment. Yes. Now, we see here and maybe we could zoom in to Article 1 on the Law on Defence, here it mentions that the law -- yes, on the application of the Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia -- so Article 1 mentions here: "The Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia will be applied on the territory of the Serb autonomous region of Krajina." This is what you told us a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we scroll down to Article 5 it provides here that the armed forces -- the armed forces of the republic -- of the SAO Krajina are the Territorial Defence and the special purpose units of the Krajina Ministry of Interior. Now, very briefly, could you tell us what is this special purpose units of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- Your Honours, these were special police units that were established in the course of spring/summer 1991 by local Serbs in the Krajina. They are sometimes colloquially referred to as the Marticevci and there is obviously, as we discussed over the previous day, yesterday, also the link with Captain Dragan, whereby Captain Dragan acted as their main trainer in the Golubic camp in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we move to Article 6 which is on the next page in the English version, yes. Here Article 6 mentions that: "The President of the Government of the SAO Krajina is by his position commander of the Territorial Defence, i.e., the armed forces of the Serb autonomous region of Krajina." So Article 6 provides the president here of a commanding position only with respect to the Territorial Defence. There is no mention here of the special purpose units of the Ministry of the Interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, but again looking at the process how all these documents were prepared at the time and also looking in -- this is discussed in the report, there was what could be qualified as a power struggle between Mr. Babic on one hand who is then president and on the other hand Mr. Milan Martic who is at that time among other things minister of the interior. I would look at the context and other documents to see who is actually de facto in command of the armed forces consisting of the TO and the -- and the special police units -- or the special purpose units of the Ministry of the Interior in official terminology.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Earlier at page 33 you mentioned that the special police units were established in the course of the spring and summer of 1991. Can you tell us roughly when were the TO units starting to be established?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, based on a review of the documents, we see the first documents -- I will rephrase that. The documents I reviewed, some of them make reference to as early as January 1991 as a time when local Serbs start -- I mean Serbs in Croatia start establishing their own TO units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is footnote 513.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that. Now, you make a reference in the next page - and I'd like us to display Exhibit L19, which is at tab 103 - you cite a decision of the Great Assembly of the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, this is on page 184 of your report, in B/C/S it would be page 223. So looking at the decision, waiting for the English version to come up, yes, Article 1 here establishes that the Territorial Defence of the region, the Serb region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem is hereby joining with the SFRY armed forces and becoming part of it. Now, before I get into the issue of the joining, have you seen any documents or other material with regard to the composition of the TO of this region, SBWS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean at -- for that period in time or -- because there is several documents, I mean, throughout the report referring to units of that TO. I'm not aware of one say overarching document that includes the total detail or the detailed structural breakdown of the units, but there are various references already prior to this date to TO -- to units of the TO of SAO SBWS.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the issue of joining, do you know whether this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, B/C/S original at the screen does not match to the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We may have to move to the right side of the screen perhaps. I apologise. Maybe you can help me because it's in Cyrillic here. Yes, I believe this is the one on the bottom right-hand side. Is that correct, Mr. Zivanovic? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now -- yes. With respect to the issue of joining the SFRY armed forces, do you know whether this decision was received or reacted by the JNA in any way?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not seen a document by the JNA or the SFRY armed forces in response to this document. Now -- and again, this may be outside the scope of the report, but you could -- one could argue what the necessity of this document is because if it would have been a recognised TO it would have been -- there would be no need to express its attachment to the TO -- to the SFRY --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Theunens, just one moment, please. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President, as the witness himself is indicating, he's going outside the report and he's speculating.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: So I would object on that ground and say that we move on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can see that -- I can see at the beginning of the answer it directly points to the fact that the expert has not seen any documents. Now, I believe that as an expert he is entitled to reach his own conclusions with respect to what is the meaning of the document or what is the meaning of the absence of documents with respect to this matter. Again, the expert is aware of what the regulations and what the doctrine provides, and I believe he is entitled to tell us what it means that a decision of this kind is issued and whether it was necessary or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, just to clarify, when I said it was outside the scope of the report, I haven't -- I meant by that that I didn't draw any particular conclusions in the report on that document. But all I wanted to mention was that given the doctrine, I mean -- and the -- for example, on the composition of the SFRY armed forces, one could question the relevance of this document because from a military point of view there was no need for such a document unless the SAO SBWS authorities want to reconfirm the attachment to what remains of the SFRY at that stage, i.e., namely Serbia and Montenegro -- okay, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Macedonia are still there but mainly Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you later say at page 189 of your report that with respect again to the TO of SAO SBWS until at least December 1991, that it was subordinated to the local Serb police under the command of Radovan Stojcic when not participating in combat operations. And here you cite to a certificate of the TO headquarters of SBWS. Perhaps we could take a look at this document. It is an admitted exhibit. It is P198.140, and that is at tab 234. Thank you. Now do you see the author of this document, as you mention in your report, is Radovan Stojcic. Before we get into the substance of the document, could you tell the Judges what was his position at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, at the time according to this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Sorry -- I'm sorry to object. We do need I believe specificity as to what time specifically is being asked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, let's start with the moment that the document was issued, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the time of the document, according to the document he is the commander of the SAO SBWS TO, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, earlier that year in 1991, are you aware of him holding any other positions or perhaps do you have any documents to that effect?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall a document - and I think that is an answer to a question in the Assembly of the Republic of Serbia, where he answers as an assistant minister of interior of the Republic of Serbia, at least an official of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia. When I say "he," I mean Radovan Stojcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And around which time was that document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know by heart, but if you can point me to the document in the amalgamated report, I would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, let me take a note and I'll try to come back to that after the break. Focusing on this document for a moment, we see that this is a certificate to certify that Slobodan Miljkovic was a volunteer in the units of the Territorial Defence since the 1st of December, 1991. And you also see the header of the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Now, could I ask you with respect to your conclusion in your report, how do you reach the conclusion that when not in combat operations the TO were at least, as you say, in December 1991 subordinated to the local Serb police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because during combat operations - and combat operations are specified by orders, I mean the start and end of combat operations - TO -- units of the TO of SBWS are fighting under JNA command. Outside combat operations there is few documents available but documents like this lead me to draw that conclusion. So in the TO -- the SBWS TO is not involved in combat operations, then we have documents like this one and then we see that the commander is Stojcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, on the issue of the Territorial Defence, I believe it is at page 189 that you make reference to the Law on the Ministries of the 25th of September. Let me just see here. While I'm pulling it up here -- yes, sorry, it starts at the bottom of page 189. You indicate here that from the 9th of October, 1991, onwards the Ministry of Defence according to the documents takes over a number of administrative tasks in relation to the local Serb TO. Can you tell us what is meant here by "administrative tasks"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these tasks are explained in the article I refer to. When you look at the Article 6 of the Official Gazette you will see these tasks, and again these are consistent with the tasks defined in Laws of Defence of the various republics when there was still -- I mean, when there was republican TOs, it has to do with manning, training, organising, and equipping.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And just before we take the break can you tell us how we reconcile these two decisions, the one we saw earlier whereby the SBWS Assembly declares that their TO is joining the SFRY armed forces and this decision where the Ministry of Defence takes over a number of administrative tasks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean at face value there is no need for reconciliation because the two documents are consistent with SFRY armed forces doctrine. But of course if you would have -- if you would go into the practical aspects, we would have to take into account that the -- it would imply -- I mean, the whole process would imply that the SFRY or what remains of SFRY recognises the SAO SBWS Territorial Defence as well as the SBWS authorities as legal authorities and who are entitled to establish a Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I believe it's the break time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Demirdjian. Thank you. Mr. Theunens, half an hour break. We will come back at 11.00. You will be escorted out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the witness is brought in, I had done some checks during the break. With respect to the document which referred to the Red Berets, the 65 ter 1179, it is in the report. It was my mistake. It is not a new document. And yes, that's it for now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: May we -- yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I was kindly reminded during the break that we should be careful to take breaks between questions and answers. And also when we're flipping pages we've been asked to turn off the microphone if at all possible so that we can hear each other's answers. I'll do my best. Just to wrap-up on the issue we were discussing earlier with respect to Badza, you were asking me if I could direct you to a portion of your report where his position is mentioned. I think it is exactly at page 189, it was the very next sentence that I think we missed which indicates now on the 31st of December, 1991, this was the time after the certificate we saw earlier he was appointed assistant minister of the interior in Serbia. Now, this is in your report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honours, this is Exhibit L11, it's an already-admitted exhibit. So I would like us now to move on to the next section of your report, page 190/191, where you deal with TO units from Serbia, and this is page 228 in the B/C/S version. And you write here at page 190 that units from Serbia took part in combat operations in Croatia such as around the town of Benkovac in Krajina as well as during the Vukovar operation. I would like you to look at a document which is 65 ter 589 at tab 170. Oh, thank you. So do we see that this document is drafted by the 1st Military District and is sent to the General Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't see the document on my monitor. I see the excerpt of my report, but maybe it's about to come. Unless I have to switch. I see it now. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: All right. Do you see it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Perfect. Now, this is, I believe, a cover page and it is sent by the 1st Military District on the 16th of November, 1991, to the General Staff. And 1st Administration, does that have any significance?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to guess -- I know the 2nd Administration was intelligence, but the first may be personnel or organisation or operations. Anyway, there are different staff administrations, but I don't recall --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the exact one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we flip to the second page in both versions, the English and the B/C/S version, here what we have is a table of the units of the units of the 1st Military District in combat operations in Eastern Slavonia. Now, do you recognise at the top of this table where you see the word "unit," at the top of each of the five columns you see the name of various units. Do you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, these are the units of the 1st Military District that are conducting operations in SBWS at that moment in time. We can see in the middle, for example, OG South, we see the 12th Corps, we see the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division, and so on, whereby it needs to be said, I think that's addressed somewhere else, that some documents at some moment in time talk about the existence of an OG North where as at other times there was a TG North, and there was also at moments in time -- certain times an OG Baranja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we turn -- I mean, the next few pages actually show the units, if I'm right, that were deployed as part of each of these organisational units; is that right? If we go to the next page, these are all the units again that are --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- part of these five main units. And if we go to page 5 and the -- both versions. Yes. Sorry, in B/C/S it's page 3. Page 5 in English, page 3 in B/C/S. Yes, we see a table here which depicts the numerical strength of the units as well as the combat equipment deployed in Eastern Slavonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you see here very specific numbers with respect to the personnel for the 1st Pgmd, the 12th Corps, OG South, et cetera, and at the bottom you see the number 20.325. What can you say about this number? And I will remind you the document is issued on the 16th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, Your Honours, I mean this number is the strength of the -- the manpower of the 1st Military District involved in operations in SBWS on the 16th of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And if we go to the very next page in both versions, here we see a table of the engagement of the Republic of Serbia TO units belonging to the 1st Military District on 15 November 1991. So again with respect to what you've written at page 190 of your report, the deployment of units of the TO of Serbia, are we to understand these are all the units that were deployed at the time from the TO of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the title says. I'm just checking whether there's no local Serb TO mentioned there. No, it seems to be okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: We can scroll down and we can also go to the next page in the English version and remain on the same page in the B/C/S version. Yes. You can look at these units as well.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So does this confirm what you were saying in your report with respect to the deployment of TO units from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And it was my impression at the time looking also now at the last page, the Kragujevac TO, I had some doubts whether Kragujevac fell in the zone of responsibility or the area covered by the 1st Military District, but in any event what we see is that units of the TO Republic of Serbia are participating in hostilities on the territory of the Republic of Croatia and they're fighting on JNA/Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And here the total number we see here is 9.000 TO units from Serbia. The previous numbers we saw was about 20.000 with respect to the other units. Would you say that this is the bulk of the units employed in Eastern Slavonia at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the document states, it reflects the strength of the force of the 1st Military District that are participating in operations in Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem at that moment in time.
