There's not much more I can conclude because I don't have the peace time strength of the 1st Military District let alone the total strength of the 1st Military District at that moment in time, so it's difficult to draw any additional conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of this page we have a title which really carries on in page 191 which is the command and control over the local Serb TO and Serb forces during the conflict in Croatia. And in your introduction here at page 191 under item 1 you start with your conclusion where you say that the example you have seen of orders and reports show a relationship between the JNA and other Serb forces which is reflective of the legislative and doctrinal framework and that they operate, as you say here, under the single command of the JNA. As a general question perhaps before we get into the specific, with respect to the non-JNA units, is there a time-period during which you could tell the Court that they operate under this single command of the JNA? Is there a time where it starts and where it ends?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: One has to look, Your Honours, at the specific documents. It's basically even if -- and also at the specific regions; for example, in southern Dalmatia where the 9th Corps is active, the JNA 9th Corps, they don't establish operational groups or tactical groups or at least not based on the documents I have reviewed, but nevertheless measures are taken to subordinate local Krajina Serb TO as well as Krajina MUP, i.e., again local Serb, under the command of units of the 9th JNA Corps, so in order to ensure a single and unified command and control. Elsewhere, more to the north, Lika, Banja, and Kordun, I mean other parts of Krajina similar orders are issued and examples are given in the report. So you have to look at -- I mean, there may have been examples, and this is often referred to I think by Mr. Seselj, for example, in the context of Eastern Slavonia, also the document we saw earlier, when he makes a statement in the parliament that, like in Borovo Selo, there we see volunteer units acting on the Serbian side against Croatian police with no -- without involvement of the JNA, so there is no subordination to the JNA. But after that, the JNA becomes involved to separate the parties and the next phase, and again then you have to look at the specific documents to see how this actually materialises on the terrain, we see that what is -- could be summarised as Serb forces, i.e., units of the local Serb TO, local Serb police, TO Serbia, volunteer/paramilitaries start operating under JNA command and control through the establishment of OGs, TGs, and as far as Vukovar is concerned also as assault detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Now, on the following pages, 192 to 194, you provide examples of combined forces acting under the direction of the JNA in the SAO of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And as of page 194 you provide examples in Western Slavonia. Since we haven't discussed Western Slavonia yet maybe we could take a look at one of the documents which emerged from that region which is 65 ter 500 at tab 143. Thank you. Now, we see here a document of the 31st of October is prepared by the 5th Corps and this is signed by Colonel Momir Talic. Are you familiar with Colonel Talic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. He was then Chief of Staff of the 5th Corps and later he becomes the command -- I mean after the creation of the VRS he becomes the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps of the VRS, so after May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the document is entitled: "Deployment and Co-ordination with TO Units." Item number 1 indicates that all TO units and staffs in areas of responsibility of JNA brigades are to be subordinated [sic] to these commands. And item number 3 indicates that the JNA brigade commanders are to consider the attached TO and other reinforcement units part of their own combat disposition. Now, what does this last item, number 3, illustrate?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means, as is also indicated, that -- it means that the JNA unit that has command over these TO units has to ensure that they are adequately supplied and also has to ensure the enforcement of all aspects of I would say military life, including military discipline, among -- military justice among these TO units. And I think you have to look at this document in the context of the document I have cited in footnote 574 on page 195, because there is a four-day time difference, but this document -- I mean the one we are looking at now, the contents refers to and attempts to provide some solutions for the difficulties and the problems that are highlighted in the document under footnote 574.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let me see if I can display that one.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I can read from my report if you want it. There are problems with "growing incidents of looting and uncontrolled behaviour of members of the TO and civilians ..." and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Theunens, we can look at it. I hadn't planned to display it but since you're mentioning it, it's 65 ter 494 at tab 139. Yes, we have it here. I'm not sure entirely to which page of the -- this document you are quoting here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's first look at the document. It's the 5th Corps operations centre. So are we talking about the same organisational unit as the previous document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. The section of the report that you're quoting --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the first page. It should be one of the following pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unless it's at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry to put you through this exercise. I believe the document is about five pages long.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. It's probably the next page. Sorry, not -- and again the next page. I mean, here they give all examples of difficulties -- I mean problems with troops and so on, but -- we'll have to move on to the next page, I believe. I mean, I'm just judging from the screen in front of me which is not always reflecting --

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I think it could be at the top of the very last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. It's still another page, next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I think we need to go to the very last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean -- I don't have the hard copy, but I'm pretty sure that what I put in my report is an adequate reflection of the document so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's go to page 6 which should be the one just previous to this one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, we have under (f), Foxtrot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. So what is your comment with respect to this excerpt?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My comment is, I drew -- I wanted to draw your attention to this document because of the document you mentioned, the 31st of October Talic order. You have to look at the Talic order in context again, I mean, this is what the analysis is about, and then the document in front of us which is the 27th of October situation report actually provides at least a number of explanations as to why it is important to consider TO units as elements of the own combat disposition. I mean, I can continue on that. When you look at again the section on Western Slavonia all documents, there was a strong presence of volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party among the local Serb TO. And there were various reports and also I think later by General Talic, indicating that at least some of these volunteers of the -- affiliated to the Serbian Radical Party were involved in the usual crimes like looting, illicit trade, and so on, and -- yeah, related crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And to tie it all in, Talic's report which is issued four days later, how do you view it with respect to this document of the 27th of October?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's in accordance with military doctrine. It means that the JNA is in command here of the operations and that means that command of the JNA unit in question is responsible -- command responsibility is responsible for the use of his forces and their behaviour and has to enforce military discipline and military justice as well as is clearly stated he's responsible also for the supply of these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation, Mr. Theunens. I would like to move now to page 197 of your report, where you indicate the forces in SBWS. You indicate first that we have OG North based -- which is based on the 12th Corps from Novi Sad. We then deal with the Guards Motorised Brigade, which you indicated to us earlier was an elite unit. Perhaps here you could expand a little bit on what you mean by the Guards Motorised Brigade being an elite unit. You briefly touched on this subject yesterday, I believe.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Without repeating what I mentioned yesterday, I mean in the references I think I put a footnote when -- this is actually earlier -- when you see on footnote 588 it refers to Articles -- at least one article, and I wrote "Armija" which is the official JNA magazine at that stage where the word "elite" is used, and there is also a reference made to the Vojni lexicon, to the SFRY military lexicon where the history as well as the various missions of the Guards Brigade, its composition, the special requirements that applied to its members and so on, I explained -- I could even add that the Guards Brigade had also the most modern equipment compared to other units in the JNA. So all that together, the level of training and so on, makes it an "elite" unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You indicate, still on page 197, that the Guards Motorised Brigade which is deployed to Vukovar on the 30th of September 1991 is the principal unit of OG South, and could you expand a little bit as to how they became the principal unit in that area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I write that they are the principal unit because the command -- so the commander and his staff and the assistant commanders of the Guards Motorised Brigade they take over the command of OG South. And when you look at the composing units of OG South after the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade not only by its manpower but also by its equipment, the Guards Motorised Brigade is the principal unit and conducting the main effort. And again, just to finalise, commanders -- I mean battalion commanders of the Guards Motorised Brigade become assault detachment commanders when the operations are conducted in Vukovar -- assault detachment commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And on the next page 198 of your report which is 237 in B/C/S, you also describe the other units that are present in that area including the 1st pgmd which we discussed before and some of the local TO units?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. And just if you allow me, I mean, I talk about OG North on page 197, the caveats I mentioned earlier, i.e., the lack of documentation at the time when these various reports were complied apply. Among the new documents, I mean the documents that became available after July 2012, reference was also made to a Tactical Group North as well as actually the 12th Corps operating as such with attached units or subordinated units without explicit reference to the name OG North, so which again highlights also the temporary nature of operational groups and tactical groups, but I didn't have that information when the amalgamated report was compiled.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, with respect to the employment of these units, I would like you to look at 65 ter 405 which is at tab 110. We see at the top on the header this is a document from the Federal Secretariat for National Defence and the document is issued on the 12th of October. I'm more interested on the next page. This page seems to describe a little bit the factual background and the situation at the time. So if we move to page 2 at the bottom of that page, I would like to take your attention to that last paragraph which states: "All armed units, be they JNA, TO, or volunteer units, must act under the single command of the JNA. They should behave and act according to the rules that apply in the army ..." et cetera, et cetera, and it is signed Blagoje Adzic. I believe this document is elsewhere in your report. Can you tell us in what context this document comes about?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a confidential letter. It's discussed on page 142 of the amalgamated report, confidential letter sent by -- or on behalf of General Blagoje Adzic, Chief of General Staff of the SFRY armed forces, and it clarifies basically -- I mean, it's a reminder of the role of the JNA in the conflict in Croatia. It also addresses how operations are conducted. And then it also explains -- I mean, it highlights again in addition to the various orders we have seen the importance of a single and unified command and control of all the forces operating on the side of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just looking at the paragraph before that, it indicates here that: "During the performance of the above tasks, any act of disobedience, indiscipline, unauthorised leaving of units, maltreatment of citizens irrespective of their nationality in the areas where units are located, plundering, looting ...," et cetera, "should be prevented at all costs." Now, having regard to the time that this document is issued, how do you assess this paragraph in the context of the letter written here by Blagoje Adzic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're looking in the context of other documents I have reviewed, and I mean by that specific orders as well as situation reports or even reports by security organs on crimes that were allegedly committed by units operating under JNA command or being present in the area where the JNA is operating during combat operations. It shows that Adzic believes that it's necessary to remind all commanders of the importance of, yes, indeed, preventing crime and so on, i.e., applying by the regulations that existed at the time, for example, in 1988 regulation on the application of the provisions of international -- the international laws of war by the SFRY armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And having regard to the specific acts that are referred to in this paragraph here, how do you view them? Is this the type of generic type of orders that would go out from the JNA leadership?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just clarify, this letter is not an order as such. I mean, there are other ways to issue orders. But it serves as a reminder to the subordinate commanders of the importance the chief of General Staff attaches to, yeah, preventing these kind of activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, this is followed three days later by another document which is 65 ter 422 at tab 117. Yes, thank you. This is a document with the header "1st Military District Command" on the 15th of October, 1991. And it is delivered to a number of units here, including the 12th Corps and the OG -- well, actually, perhaps you could clarify the translation here. It says operations group JUG, J-u-g, at the top of the document where it says deliver immediately. Can you clarify that for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, Jug stands for south, Operation Group South.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: So that's the term used in the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Looking at this order, this time this is an order from the 1st Military District, you see the first item which is: "Establish full control in the AOR of the units ..." And the second item here says that: "All paramilitary compositions and the volunteer detachments which refuse to put themselves under the command of the JNA units are to be removed from the territory." Now, does this follow from what you were telling us earlier in the document we saw three days before with respect to singleness of command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, yes. I mean, this is clearly a link, one follows from the other. So General Panic received a letter of General Adzic, and I think the last paragraph of the letter we haven't discussed here but states that the information contained in the letter should be communicated to all the troops. From a military point of view then, it's logical that the subordinate commander in this case, Colonel-General Panic, commander of the 1st Military District, issues an order to his subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we go to the last page in both documents, yes -- well, it's probably the bottom of the page in the B/C/S, okay. It is issued by Panic himself. Very well. I would like us now to move to the Vukovar operation which I believe would be -- or practically if we move to the Mrksic part of your report at page 438 onwards. Now, earlier if you'll remember we saw a document of the 12th Corps from the month of October which was a retrospective document. It is P1686 which discussed the deployment of the 12th Corps units since the 4th of May. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, Your Honours, and if I remember well that was also one of the new documents I didn't have available when, I mean, the Vukovar report was compiled I think in 2003 or 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment. I would like us to pull up 65 ter 6198 which is at tab 665. And this is one of the new documents, Your Honours. Thank you. Now, this is a document of the 12th Corps on the 8th of July, 1991, and the title is: "Order for Deployment for 12th Corps Forces in Slavonia." Now, we see the initial paragraph again provides the situational -- the context basically. And if we scroll down to the bottom of the page, item number 2, it says: "I have decided: The 12th Corps forces ...," and he names three brigades here, "shall advance through Slavonia in two marching columns in Slavonia and one in Baranja on the following axes ...," and he provides the number of axes here. "The objective is to prevent by a rapid and energetic movement of armoured and mechanised equipment on the given axes in a show of force ..." et cetera, et cetera. Now, first of all, could you tell us a little bit about the axes that are described here? You have Odzaci, Bogojevo, Osijek, et cetera, and all the other ones.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ideally one would look at the map to see the terrain because these axes of approach or advance are based on the availability of the roads and the nature of the terrain, i.e., where troops could move from east to west in order to deploy -- I mean, to move into Eastern Slavonia and Baranja, but even to move further because mention is made from of Slavonski Brod, Novi Gradiska, Kutina, and so on, so these are general directions to move from east to west.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. So this is not restricted to Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we would have to look at other parts of the document because it doesn't -- this just indicates how -- I mean in which direction they should move, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I think it -- maybe other parts of the document include what should be done in which location.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, if we move to page 2 actually we will see here -- and I think that in B/C/S it's the bottom of page 1 for now. Here you see the mention of the 17th Corps which have been engaged in Slavonia, I think you mentioned this earlier --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In B/C/S we can now move to the next page. And you see the axes are being a bit more specific here on this page.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And towards the bottom of that page, if we scroll down a little bit --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: -- we see the formation of a tactical group in Baranja as well.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, yes. But clearly -- I mean, in these paragraphs you see the missions of the subordinate units and then on the basis of locations are indicated you can conclude that it -- the order covers more than only Eastern Slavonia and -- yeah. Because for Baranja, for example, it states -- I mean what I can read here that the 1st Mechanised Battalion shall be -- in the Beli Manastir sector shall be ready to secure axes leading from Hungary into Baranja, so they should be ready to move further to the border or at least control the northern border area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at the time could you tell us, based on the documents that you have seen, what are the general objectives of the JNA with respect to these movements?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one hand there is an order from September from the 1st Military District which should be discussed in the report which basically talks about moving from east to west but up to the area north of Zagreb, i.e., from Eastern Slavonia -- from Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, through Western Slavonia, all the way to the north-western border with Hungary. That is one information. On the other hand, of course, the evolving combat situation, we notice - but this is after this document - that following the fall of Vukovar on the 18th of November, I mean the surrender of the Croatian forces there, that basically on the 23rd of November a cease-fire agreement is concluded in Geneva between the parties and under the auspices of the UN, and this means the end of the operations. So the -- at that stage the JNA is satisfied with achieving control over a number of areas but not -- I mean, these -- that situation is not the same as the one that was projected in the September 1st Military District order, i.e., they have achieved control over areas considered Serb except for Western Slavonia where there's still a significant Serb presence north of the area under the control of the JNA. But, for example, the JNA has not achieved control over the area between Eastern Slavonia -- or between Baranja, Eastern Slavonia, Western Srem as an eastern limit and Western Slavonia as a western limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we move to the next page, page 3 in both English and the B/C/S version, I'd like you to focus on item number 10 here, where we see that the -- yes. We see here that the 12th Corps KM is in Novi Sad and the 12th Corps IKM is in Tenja village. Could you just describe very briefly those abbreviations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, KM stands for command post, so the "komanda mjesta," and IKM is the forward command post. Novi Sad is located in Serbia and Tenja is located in Eastern Slavonia, in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry. Very well. Yes, this is one of the new documents, Your Honour, 65 ter 6198. May I apply to tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1687. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like us to look at an admitted exhibit which is D13 at tab 494, please. Now, the previous document we saw was the 8th of July, the deployment of the 12th Corps. And this one should be -- yes, the 27th of July. It is issued by the 2nd Mechanised Battalion. Yes. Now, this document reports that a conflict broke out in the morning between the Serbian population and Croatian MUP forces in Erdut and its surroundings. And under item 4 we see that the report says: "I have decided to march along the village of Miletic, village of Bogojevo Most," which is the bridge, "Novi Erdut...," et cetera, "to separate the conflicting sides." Now, you've seen this document before, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go to page 3 in the English version, it should be page 2 in B/C/S, it is signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Mirko Broceta. I was just wondering if you have seen any other documents issued by Mr. Broceta, because the header of this document does not indicate to which unit this mechanised battalion belongs to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have -- sorry. I may have seen documents signed by Broceta, but I think when you look at the other documents the -- this is the 2nd Battalion of the 51st Mechanised Brigade, which was a unit of the 12th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the 51st Mechanised Brigade was actually referred to in the document of the 8th of July that we just saw; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, you have -- as I just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, following this one, I would like you to look at 65 ter 6199 which is at tab 666.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And this is, Your Honours, one of the new documents. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this is issued by the command of the 12th Corps on the 9th of August, 1991. You've had an opportunity to review this document, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I mean, at face value I don't recognise it, but let's go through the document and then maybe then --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. It is a report on the armed conflict near the village of Dalj on the 1st of August --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I saw that. Sorry, I remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in the initial paragraphs there is a report on the conflict on the 1st of August. It describes fierce conflict between armed forces of the MUP, ZNG, and the organised Serbian forces in the village of Dalj.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The second paragraph indicates that due to the conflict there are many dead and wounded. And two paragraphs below, the one that begins with: "Given the situation in the village ... and the endangered position of the area ... the commander of the 51st Mechanised Brigade reported to the commander of the 12th Corps and submitted to him a detailed report, emphasizing the need for deploying parts of the unit to separate the warring parties. And after receiving authorisation at 5.45, the commander of the 12th Corps ordered the units of the 51st Mechanised Brigade to move out and separate the warring parties." Now, with respect to this paragraph we see a back and forth between the 51st Mechanised Brigade and the 12th Corps. And could you comment on this exchange?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the normal implementation of command and control in a sense that the subordinate unit commander, i.e., the commander of the 51st Brigade reports to his commander, i.e., the commander of the 12th Corps, about the situation in his zone of responsibility. And as a subordinate commander he can make proposals to the superior commander as to what he sees or what he considers as the most suitable course of action to adopt. And he will be allowed -- no, and he can implement that or he will implement that course of action after receiving an order to do so from his superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And that is what -- the last sentence here says that: "After receiving authorisation, ... the commander of the 12th Corps ordered that the 51st Mechanised Brigade ..." Who would have given the authorisation to the 12th Corps?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that would have come from the superior command of the 12th Corps, which was the command of the 1st Military District at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And if we go to the last page of this document, it should be page 3 and probably page 2 in the B/C/S version, yes we see again here that the document is signed by Chief of Staff Colonel Srboljub Trajkovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now -- and again you -- I think you explained this to us earlier that the Chief of Staff is authorised to issue such orders -- well, this is a report actually, I'm sorry. But ...

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned -- I mean the chief -- based on doctrine, the Chief of Staff is the only one who can replace the commander and can act on his behalf. This is, for example, explained in the regulation on the light -- on the infantry mountain and other brigades -- I think it's from 1984 and it's quoted in the Vukovar report but also in the Karadzic part 1 I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document was 65 ter 6199, it's a new document. Might I apply to tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1688. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to move to page 442 of your report, which is the section coming from the Mrksic report. And here you explain this page and the following pages the operations in seizing Vukovar involving various units. First here you -- and you've said this before, that the Guards Motorised Brigade, the gmtbr is resubordinated from the SSNO to the 1st Military District, this is on the 29th of September, and I believe we have the order copied here in the report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I just wanted to bring your attention to the wording here. It says the Guards Motorised Brigade, except the security battalion, is resubordinated to the 1st front command. Do you have any comments on the usage of this language here, front command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it must be a lapsus. I don't have the original B/C/S in front of me but it's most -- I mean, it's clearly the 1st Military District command because we can also see from the various reports and orders issued by OG South on the one hand and the 1st Military District on the other hand, that is that all confirming that the Guards Motorised Brigade is subordinated to the 1st Military District during the time it is participating in the combat operations in the wider Vukovar area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise. I should have given the B/C/S equivalent. It's page 496 in the B/C/S version, otherwise we can always pull up the document. And we may have to move to the next page to see the text of the order. This is the header. Yes. I don't know if that helps you at all?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean the word "vojista" is uncommon -- I mean, I find it uncommon based on the documents I reviewed but I think the matter is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like us to look at two orders which were issued by the 12th Corps. The first one is at 65 ter 5992 which is tab 542. Yes. Thank you. Now, this is a document of the 20th of September, and we see here that here this is an order to 12th Corps to attack. So this is issued by the 12th Corps command. Can you explain to me -- I mean, we have seen this before in other documents. We see that the 1:100.000 and a number of villages are listed here. What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this refers to the maps and like, for example, what we discussed in the previous document, that is, if avenues of approach or axes of attack or something are identified in an order, they are also visualised on a map which makes it much easier for the subordinate commanders to understand the orders from their commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Can we move to page 2 in English. In B/C/S we'll have to move to the bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, quite right. It is one of the new documents. Didn't I actually mention that? No. So looking at this document here, we see that the 12th Corps and in brackets we see a number of units, brigades, TO units, et cetera, and even TO detachments, shall carry out an offensive operation along the general Osijek-Nasice-Virovitica axis. Their task to crush Ustasha units, lift the blockade of units and military installations, et cetera, et cetera. Now, within the context of -- well, the document is issued on the 20th of September. Can you tell us based on the documents you have seen, what is -- what are the operations carried out by the JNA at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this order actually refers to -- Your Honours, to what I mentioned earlier what is -- I will find a reference for the 1st Military District order in September that talks about JNA units and subordinate units advancing from east to west up to the borders with Hungary, i.e., through Western Slavonia up to the north-western border of Croatia with Hungary. And -- because you see the axis -- I mean, mention is made they have to advance in the direction of -- oops, I touched the screen, but in the direction of Bjelovar. And then -- I mean, before that, all the subordinate units are listed, including a number of TO detachments. So at that time the goal is still to move -- I mean, based on these two documents, to move up to the -- to advance up to the borders with Hungary north-west, i.e., to restore SFRY authority over Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the sentence below that describes the 453rd Mechanised Brigade to remain within the security and intelligence command of Vukovar and co-ordinate the activities of all forces in, and we'll go to the next page, in that area. And the next sentence here says: "Once the right conditions are in place, launch an offensive operation in order completely to lift the blockade of Vukovar, Borovo, and Borovo Naselje and destroy Ustasha units." Can you tell us again what is this -- what does it mean by requesting to lift the blockade of Vukovar? What is it a reference to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initial official objective for us to lift the blockade of the JNA barracks in Vukovar which had been blocked by Croats in the course of the month of August and I understand -- I mean, we will see that probably later that on the basis of -- I mean documents of OG South that by the 6th of October OG South units reach the JNA barracks in Vukovar and lift the blockade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: If we go to page 4 in English which is page 3 in B/C/S, I want you to look at item 5.2 which is entitled at the bottom of that page in English "blockade forces." It indicates here that: The 453rd Mechanised Brigade with a number of TO detachments shall impose a blockade of Vukovar and together with territorially based units, once the right conditions have been created, it shall launch an attack with the objective of breaking up the Ustasha forces, et cetera, et cetera. Can you perhaps, again within the context of the time-period, tell us what is meant here by imposing a blockade of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, given the fact that Vukovar is a major city and the complexity of urban warfare whereby in very simplistic term cities are much easier to defend than to conquer, the most appropriate way the JNA commander believes or considers to restore JNA control, i.e., to lift the blockade of the barracks would be to isolate the city, i.e., to block it in order to prevent the influx of Croatian reinforcements or Croatian resupply, and by thus weakening the forces defending Vukovar it would be easier to achieve the goals set by the JNA, consisting first and foremost -- first of all of lifting the blockade of the barracks; and then, as it indicated here also, breaking up the "Ustasha forces" whereby "Ustasha" is the name used to identify members of the Croatian National Guard and other Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And there's one last item I'd like you to look at and it is at page -- at page 7 of the English version, and it should be page 6 in B/C/S. Let's scroll down to the bottom of that page. Now, this is the section dealing with moral and psychological support. You see there's a section here -- a paragraph which begins with: "Lifting the blockade of JNA barracks and garrisons ..." et cetera. And the last sentence here reads: "In the area of combat operations, work with the authorities and people who are loyal to the JNA." Again, based on the material that you have seen, do you have a view as to what this is referring to, authorities and people who are loyal to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a bit -- I don't see it on my screen. I mean, I can hear what you tell me, but I would like to see it --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: At the very bottom of that page do you see, it starts with: "In the area of combat operations ..."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I would say it's a bit of a complex matter because at face value you would say okay the authorities -- you could conclude these are the SAO SBWS authorities, but then again it would be -- make more sense to look into wider context and look also at the instructions and orders of the 1st Military District in this context as well as OG South because one sees that there is occasions at least, and again based on the documents I reviewed, a difference in attitude of the 12th Corps on the one hand and on the other hand the 1st Military District and OG South and the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division towards SAO SBWS self-established authorities. That's one point. And secondly, well, people who are loyal to the JNA, the obvious conclusion would be that that refers to the local Serb TO. But again, I think we -- as I try also to do in the report is to look at as many documents -- I mean, the available documentation in order really to be in a good position to draw conclusions as to just restrict myself to one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Before I move on, Your Honours, this was a new document 65 ter 5992. Might I apply to tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1689. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I'd like you to look at a second document here from the 12th Corps, it is 65 ter 5997, tab 544, which is also a new document. Thank you. Now, we see that this is a document issued eight days after the one we just saw, so this is the 28th of September, 1991. Command of the 12th Corps, village of Dalj -- in fact, just on that point earlier the document we saw on the 8th of July established that the command of the 12th Corps was in Novi Sad and that the IKM, so the forward command post, was in Tenja. Do you have any information as to what is -- what is a reference here to the village of Dalj?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean a command post, whether it's the main command post or the forward command post, I mean to be safe I would say the forward command post of the 12th Corps is now located in Dalj, which corresponds with the development of the situation on the ground, i.e., that by end of September Dalj is under JNA control -- actually, early already but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, under the word "urgent," you see that there is a preliminary sentence: "In order to organise and replace forces currently holding Vukovar under siege from the north and the west, I hereby order ..." And here we see that Colonel Milan Belic is appointed commander of the Operations Group North. And the following units are subordinated to him and it's a mixed bag of TO units and detachments as well as mechanised battalion here. Now, earlier you mentioned the issue of operation groups and tactical groups. First of all, is there a difference between both formations, an OG and a TG?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the doctrine, an OG would be larger and a TG would be the smaller unit, and I can -- we can go to the section in the report. Now what we see in Vukovar is that the names -- I mean that the OGs as they are established or the TGs do not necessarily reflect the doctrinal -- I mean from the size point of view, they don't -- do not necessarily reflect what is in doctrine. If I'm not mistaken a bit -- an operational group could involve several brigades, a tactical group several battalions, well we see that, for example, this operational group is actually a battalion plus, so which highlights also the importance of looking at the specific documents. But the other key aspects of OGs and TGs, i.e., that they unify JNA, TO, and other units operating on the side of the JNA, this is supported by this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, the next sentence here deals with the OG commander's tasks, which is to consolidate forces north of Vukovar, blocking exit from Vukovar from the north, and preparing the lift -- to lift the siege of Vukovar. Now, am I right in -- since -- well, OG North itself, what is the area that is covered by OG North?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean -- you mean this OG North that is ordered in this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, generally -- well, actually, no. We've seen the orders from the 12th Corps as well as to the area that is covered, and I suspect from your answer that there is not an area that is covered at all times by this OG, so if you expand on that a little.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to highlight it would be misleading -- I mean, in my view at least the OG North that is specified in the document here in front of us is not what is commonly understood as OG North, i.e., the operational group that is responsible for -- that was responsible for a large part of Baranja and the northern part of Eastern Slavonia up to the Vuka river. So basically the JNA forces deployed around Vukovar. There was one group of units responsible for the northern part and the other was responsible for the southern part, whereby OG South was responsible for the southern part, and for the northern part we had the 12th Corps as part of the wider OG North, and here we have a smaller OG North that is established at one moment in time. At another moment in time you will see a Tactical Group North being defined which generally -- I mean they are responsible for the area north of the Vuka river.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the very next sentence here: "Ensure the existence of a physical connection with OG South which is launching operations from the village of Negoslavci."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Would this relate to what you've told us earlier about the difficulty between these units to connect each other, and you were talking about the bridges and the entry points, I believe, at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually we're now looking at the area basically surrounding Vukovar on the north, the west, and the south. The JNA tries to maintain a blockade of Vukovar to, as I mention, prevent resupply of the Croatian defence forces within Vukovar. Nevertheless - and again this is not an issue I addressed in my report but it is common knowledge - in spite of this blockade that was imposed by the JNA, the Croats managed to send in reinforcements and get out troops and so on into Vukovar. And in order to -- I mean it's essential if you want to enforce a siege, a physical siege or a blockade of a city, you need to avoid gaps between your forces and you avoid a gap even if the terrain there isn't entirely flat, you avoid a gap by establishing a physical connection, for example, that you see each other or that you have a common check-point or patrols meet up between the various units that are ensuring the blockade of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is 65 ter 5997, might I apply to tender it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1690. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I believe that it's the time for the break, Your Honours, before I move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: A few minutes early but that's no problem, Mr. Demirdjian. Second break, Mr. Theunens. We'll come back at 12.45. You will be escorted, as usual, out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, before the break the last document we saw related to OG North was dated the 28th of September and in your report still at page 442 which we were looking at earlier you indicated that the guards Motorised Brigade was resubordinated to the 1st Military District on the next day, the 29th of September, 1991. I would like us to look at page 443 of your report which in the B/C/S version is page 497, where you have a diagram of the forces deployed in the area.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, if we first zoom in to the upper diagram, you have what you call here a graphic representation of the 1st Military District after the resubordination of the Guards Motorised Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. And just to clarify, these are diagrams I drew myself, Your Honours, on -- based on various sources of information. The purpose was just to highlight the fact that the Guards Motorised Brigade was subordinated to the 1st Military District at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, if we scroll down to the next diagram in the English version, I think in the B/C/S you may have to turn to the next page, here we have a diagram of the 1st Military District, now the difference being this time you don't have the 4th Corps, 17th Corps, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Indeed, I mean, we will have to look at the subtitle. Basically here I only focus on the units that are participating in the operations in Eastern Slavonia. And just to come back to something I said before the break, I spoke about the 1st Military District order of September 1991 with the wider mission of restoring territorial integrity for the JNA, i.e., moving from the east to the west, that was the document that is mentioned in footnote 1488. We don't have to see it but just I want to correct. I spoke about the 1st Military District order of September 1991. It's in footnote 88. It's order 5-89.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Now here we see Operative Group South which is highlighted in yellow. I don't know if we could zoom in a little bit more for visibility purposes. Thank you. And here you've written OG South Colonel Mile Mrksic and gmtbr Colonel Mile Mrksic. Could you just explain to us how is it that Mrksic appears under both headers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I refer to what I mentioned earlier, that is, that the command of OG South is basically taken over by the command of Guards Motorised Brigade within a week after the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade in Vukovar, and we can see that from the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade as also the various orders issued by Colonel Mile Mrksic after the 6th of October, 1991, where he signs or which he signs as commander of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Next we see the 80th Motorised Brigade, and just to be -- well, we may see documents later about this, but could you already tell us when the 80th Motorised Brigade becomes involved in the Vukovar operation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it's in the course of October, but I'm not sure. I would have to see the specific document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: That's fine. We will come to that. And then finally we see TO Vukovar, Miroljub Vujovic. The fact that you've put the name here indicates that this is the man who led the TO Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least he was -- I'm sorry. At least he was identified in a number of documents as commander or chief sometimes even of the local Serb TO Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. I would like to take you to page 448 of your report. In this section you deal with the -- well, in the previous pages you were dealing with the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade. Here we have the order for blockade and attack of the 1st of October. And at page 449 which is the very next page you have a paragraph about the capture of the barracks. Now, you mentioned the capture of the barracks earlier. Could you tell us how significant was it for the Guards Motorised Brigade to capture the barracks?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as we saw from the documents we have discussed before the break, lifting the blockade of the barracks was one of the objectives of the JNA's combat operations in Vukovar area at that moment in time, blockade of the barracks in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And you say one of the objectives. After the capture of the JNA barracks, did combat operations carry on?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Operations were continued and then we come to the missions as we discussed also in the documents before the break is to advance -- I mean to capture Vukovar and also then to advance with the forces further west from Eastern Slavonia towards Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Can we look at 65 ter 460 which is at tab 129. Thank you. This is an order of the 1st Military District of the 19th of October, so this is after the capture of the barracks. And if we look at the cover page here it is delivered to the 12th Corps, 1st pgmd. We see OG South again which is written as Jug, et cetera. And if we go to page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S versions, and if we scroll to the bottom of that page, you will see here that the 1st Military District orders the 12th Corps, and this is at the very bottom of the page, and OG South to establish a full close blockade of Vukovar and with the 1st pgmd a blockade in depth ... et cetera. So again, does this confirm what you were telling us a minute ago that combat operations carry on in the middle of October? And if we move to page 3 in both versions, please and let's look at item number 4. Here the 1st Military District writes the following: "In order to prevent looting, the abuse of citizens, and murder, even that of captives, all armed persons and groups which are not in the JNA and TO composition are to be disarmed and detained and the leaders incarcerated and legal measures taken against them." Now, having regards to military doctrine and regulations, could you tell us how typical is an order of this kind?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- I mean, without having to go through the whole document, but paragraph 4 actually follows from paragraph 3 in this document where General Panic highlights a number of incidents which -- and are related to poor discipline. From the various documents I have reviewed, there are problems with discipline, in particular among members of local Serb TO and of volunteer units, and these problems with discipline also express themselves in criminal behaviour towards civilians in acts like looting and so on. We have seen a few documents. And because of this, General Panic as the commander of the 1st Military District, i.e., the highest commander, operational commander in the area, reminds his subordinate commanders of their responsibilities in order to enforce discipline and also prevent criminal activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You've quoted this -- for the record this document at page 453/454 of your report. I would like to take you now to 459 where you indicate here that the -- that during combat operations the local Territorial Defence is subordinated to the OG South. And looking at this I would like us to take a look at 65 ter 496, which is at tab 140. Yes, thank you. This is a decision issued by OG South on the 29th of October, 1991, and it is a decision on the continuation of the assault operation Vukovar. Under item 1 here we see that the first stage includes the capture of Mitnica. And under item 2 is a description of the structure of assault detachments, JOds. Now, we didn't look at it in detail in the earlier part of the report, but could you quickly describe to us what is an assault detachment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, assault detachments apply the same principles as tactical -- as operational groups and tactical groups, albeit they existed at a much lower level. They are, for example, established when conducting warfare in urban areas by the JNA. And again, looking at the OG South documents that mention assault detachments, we see that assault detachments consist of JNA battalions or elements of JNA battalions, local Serb TO, elements of the TO Serbia, as well as volunteer or members of or elements of volunteer units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in this JOd-1 we see the structure, a motorised battalion, and then we see a detachment, Leva Supoderica, and a detachment Petrova Gora, are these the two TO units we were discussing earlier today?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And we see a number of other companies, volunteer companies, et cetera. And just briefly if we can go to the next page in the English version, we also see other detachments, the 2nd, the 3rd, the 4th, the 5th, et cetera. Now, you told us earlier that they are similar to the OGs or TGs although on a smaller level. Who would be heading these assault detachments on the ground?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular context of the assault detachments established by OG South, I've included a diagram on page 458 which shows that it's -- commanders of motorised battalions of the Guards Motorised Brigade who are commanders of these assault detachments and this is, for example, the case with then-Major Borivoje Tesic who is the commander of the 1st Assault Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps we could go to page 458 of your report, display that on the screen. It should be page 505 in the B/C/S version. Yes, thank you. So here again we see OG South Commander Mile Mrksic at the top of this structure, and I believe you have included the various assistants to the commander here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, you have on one hand the staff and on the other hand you have the assistant commanders and the branches I explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just to be clear here, we have the assistant commander for political affairs, for security, for logistics. Is this just a sample or are there more assistants to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are the assistant commanders. The other departments or branches are part of the staff and they are organised and managed by the Chief of Staff who is also the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. You mentioned earlier Borivoje Tesic. We see him under assault detachment 1, and so it is under his detachment that the Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora were deployed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I prefer the word "employed," because "deploy" is just to put troops on the ground, but they were used, according to this order, under his command, and that's also visible, for example, in the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I apologise, yeah. And this graphic representation as you've indicated in your report is based on order 235-1 which is footnoted in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, at least for the structures concerned and the names I added on the basis of other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names of commanders, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to the end of combat operations. Your report includes a number of detailed orders and reports during the month of October and November, so I will not delve into it at this stage. And I would like to take you to page 467 of your report under item number 22. And here you quote I believe it is from the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade a conversation between Mile Mrksic on the 18th of November, and this is with the envoy of the Croatian Democratic Union for Vukovar. We don't see his name here but it is elsewhere in the report. Do you remember who -- the name of the envoy?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to remember if it's Mr. Marin Vidic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, in fact at page 472 you mention it, but we will get to that later. And according to the diary you indicate here that the commander of OG South requested the unconditional surrender and guaranteed safety of Ustasha forces in accordance with the Geneva Conventions. So this is directly from the war diary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in addition to the diary we have an OG South report which is 65 ter 606, Your Honours, that's at tab 507. I would like us to display this document. It is not a new document, but I don't believe that it is included in your report, Mr. Theunens. We'll look at it in a moment now. Yes. It's the Operative Group South's confidential number 423-1. Do you see it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It is sent to the 1st Military District and to the SSNO cabinet. It's a regular combat report and we have here a mention that at about 1.40 in the morning the commissioner of the government for Vukovar Marin Vidic asked to talk with OG Jug commander. They spoke twice, around 8.00 and 9.00, when the conditions were set for the surrender of Ustasha forces. Then the next paragraph deals with negotiations held at Mitnica around 9.50 in the morning. What is -- can you tell us briefly what is Mitnica and what was there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mitnica is a neighbourhood in Vukovar close to the centre, and I understand from the other documents that on the 18th of November Croatian forces in Mitnica surrendered to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And is this consistent with the war diary that you quoted in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can go to the last page, Your Honours. We can see here that it is -- well, let's see the original. Yes. It is issued by Colonel Mile Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, this is a document that is not in the report. May I seek to tender it, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1691. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at page 470 of your report you mention the Zagreb Agreement, and you explain that an evacuation agreement was reached between the JNA, the Croatian government, and international organisations, including the ICRC and the Medecins Sans Frontieres in relation to the sick and wounded from the hospital. What you mention here at page 471 of your report is that there is no mention in the evacuation agreement of the JNA handing over evacuees to any other body of authority. Now, could you explain to us in principle what happens in the military should the army leadership reach an agreement at the international level, what did they do with that agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would expect, Your Honours, that the agreement that is reached at the highest level is then translated into specific orders for the various units that may play a role or that are likely to play a role in implementing that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, the agreement is admitted as P1461. Have you seen any documents based on what you just said from the military leadership around that time with respect to the agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, and I've also explained that on the bottom of page 471 -- 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Could I ask that we display 65 ter 610 which is at tab 175. And this is a reference to a document that you discuss at page 472 of your report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the interpreters have the reference for the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: For the report that is page 532.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, do you see the document, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, this is a document from the 1st Military District being sent to a number of units, again including the 12th Corps, pgmd, OG South, et cetera. If we scroll down a little bit at page 1 of the English version, the first sentence we see here is: "The Croatian armed forces are defeated in the area of combat operations carried out by the 1st Military District units." Now, having regard to the time and the date, is this a document which roughly marks the end of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's maybe a matter of nuance, but indeed by then the JNA has achieved control over Vukovar, but as we see from subsequent situation reports there is -- the surrender is still ongoing. There may still be small resistance pockets that have to be eliminated first before combat operations can be really described as having finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Well, on that note if we move to page 2, we can remain on page 1 in the B/C/S version, you see the -- under the title "Order," OG South: "Carry out detailed and complete preparations and in co-ordinated action with TG North take the hospital and the MUP building and mop-up the remaining Ustasha forces ..." So is this a reference to what you were just saying now, there are small pockets still that need to be captured?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually, what I was saying is referring more to paragraphs 2 and following. At least based on this single document when you look in the context and of course there are documents that -- JNA documents that state that there are "Ustashas" in the hospital, then obviously I would agree with you. But looking just at the document in isolation there is no reference to resistance pockets in relation to the hospital. But, for example, the second paragraph that refers to Tactical Group North talks about mopping up remaining Ustasha forces. So that's what I meant by resistance pockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification. If we move to page 4 in the English which is page 3 in the B/C/S version, I'd like us to zoom on item number 8 in the middle of that page where the 1st Military District reminds that every unit has to control the situation on their territory, that commanders at all levels will be responsible for this. And he carries on saying that: "War time laws have not entered into force and therefore - as always - nobody has the right to retribution and other kinds of revenge, which some local TO units carried out." Now, how do you interpret this last sentence, especially with respect to the end of the sentence "carried out"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this paragraph indicates that General Panic is very concerned about the behaviour of members of local Serb TO who, based on his information and what he puts here in his order to his subordinate commanders, have been involved in criminal behaviour before and that criminal behaviour includes - I'm just reading from the document - acts of retribution or retribution and other kinds of revenge. So it makes sense -- since this has happened, it makes sense for Panic to remind his subordinate commanders to prevent such behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, when subordinate commanders receive such a reminder, again based on the military doctrine, what do military commanders do at that moment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, based on one hand of the principles of command and control and, more specifically, the two principles of unity of command and the principle of the obligation to implement decisions, and on the other hand their understanding of the applicable regulations like I mean the Geneva Conventions and others as they are described in the 1988 regulations on the implementation of the international laws of war, a subordinate JNA commander, i.e., a subordinate of Panic, would issue orders to his subordinates in order to ensure that Panic's warning and instructions are implemented. In addition, he would also verify the implementation of these orders -- of his orders, I'm sorry, and report accordingly to Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In practical terms, are you able to tell us how would he verify that these orders are implemented?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, inspection is a function of command and control. The whole reporting system is one important aspect of implementing the inspection function, i.e., subordinate units on a regular basis report not only about their situation but also about the level of implementation of the orders they have received. In addition, the commander can also inspect himself, he can use staff officers to go on the terrain and to look around and to see how things are going and to what extent, for example, the reports he receives from his subordinate units correspond with reality. He can use the military police, in particular the Guards Motorised Brigade since they had two battalions of military police compared to only one battalion for regular brigades, so these military police can be used to send -- to patrol and to make sure that -- I mean the orders from the commander in this specific regard, i.e., enforcing discipline, preventing crimes, are abided by, are implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Along these lines I would like you to look at a new document which is 65 ter 5991 at tab 541. Yes. This is a document of the command of the 12th Corps, which is another one of the subordinated units of the 1st Military District. It's issued on the 22nd of November and the preliminary paragraph says that: "Due to an increase in the number of incidents of undisciplined conduct and disobedience ..." et cetera, et cetera, "I hereby order." Could you look at item number 3 which says: "We have information that certain officers take it upon themselves to pass judgement on prisoners on the spot, which is impermissible." Now, this is the command of the 12th Corps. Again, based on your previous answer could you tell us how would the command of the 12th Corps have obtained this type of information?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would probably be unlikely that a superior -- because I have -- I mean, we have had this over the years in the ICTY, the translation of "staresine." I mean I am not a translator, but it makes more sense to translate as "superior," it's not just only officers but any superior, somebody in a position of authority. Anyway, they're not going to -- probably not going report it themselves, but as I mentioned earlier, the commander, and we saw that also yesterday, the commander has to be familiar with the situation two levels down, he has various tools to do so. When I spoke about reporting system and military police, I didn't mention the security organs, but -- I mean, there are various tools available to him to allow himself to familiarise himself with the situation of his units two levels down, including their potential alleged involvement in crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And do I understand it correctly that you're pointing to a small error in the translation when you talked about "staresine"?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, when I was here it was a long debate and it was never clarified, so I don't know what the situation is now. I left here four years ago, but when I look at military doctrine not all "st aresine" are officers. "Staresine" actually would mean in my understanding superior and not all superiors are officers. An officer is most often a superior but it -- I mean it doesn't go both ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it doesn't change the sense of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And superiors, are you saying that they would not necessarily mean officers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, because an NCO can also be in the position of a superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I understand. And if we go to the next page, we can stay on the same page and scroll down in the B/C/S version, this is a document issued by Andrija Biorcevic, so that was the commander of the 12th Corps at the time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a new document, I wish to tender it. But considering the remark Mr. Theunens has made just now, I will submit it for a revised translation so perhaps at this time we may MFI it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, MFI it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1692 marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, at page 471 at the bottom of that page of your report which in the B/C/S version is page 531 you comment, again moving back to the Zagreb agreement, that there is, again, no reference to this agreement in the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade. I take it from this that you have reviewed the war diary which is footnoted in your report in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did at the time also for the Vukovar case, so I'm familiar with the war diary --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the last sentence on this page begins with: "Taking into account the level at which the evacuation agreement was conducted with the involvement of international organisations, it can be considered unusual that such references are lacking in the gmtbr war diary ..." So here you're making a connection with the fact that the agreement was reached at the international level, and am I correct in understanding from this conclusion of yours that you would have expected to see this in the war diary?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, given the purpose of a war diary -- and maybe there wouldn't be a specific reference to the Zagreb Agreement, but what I said earlier that the superior command - and that would be at the level of the Supreme Command Staff or the General Staff - would have issued orders on the basis of the Zagreb Agreement to the 1st Military District, and then the 1st Military District would have issued orders to the -- to its units not just to take the hospital, as we have seen, but then also to handle those present in the hospital and treat them in accordance with the Zagreb Agreement. And I haven't seen any written documents to that effect. The only thing we see is later on in daily situation reports there are general references made by OG South as well as the 1st Military District that the evacuation of the population is conducted in accordance with Geneva Conventions and the relevant regulations without explicitly referring to the people in -- who are present at the hospital before the JNA entered or members of the Guards Motorised Brigade entered the hospital or before they were handed over to members of the local Serb TO in Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in previous trials I believe it is correct to say that you have seen the video on the 20th of November where on one of the Vukovar bridges you see an exchange between a JNA officer and one of the international monitors. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Actually, I remember two videos. There is one showing a representative of the ICRC and General Pavkovic who had been sent from the SSNO as a -- I think liaison officer to the Guards Motorised Brigade. And there is also the -- I mean, the video showing the conversation between, again, the representative of the ICRC and Major Veselin Sljivancanin, who was the assistant commander of security of the Guards Motorised Brigade and who was in charge of the actual evacuation on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Might I ask that we show one of these two videos. It's 65 ter 5006 at tab 687. I believe that the interpreters have a translation, although part of the conversation is in English, part of it is in B/C/S. Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Tell us. "Nicholas Borsinger: Not to help fighters disguise themselves as civilians and be evacuated from the hospital. "Interpreter: The role of the Red Cross is not to help those who are fighting to escape the hospital as civilians.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
