utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Then why don't they allow us to do our job. "Interpreter: Why don't you leave us to do our job? "Nicholas Borsinger: I -- I -- I'm never to going to prevent you from doing your job!

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Does he want to control the army? "Nicholas Borsinger: He can check -- if he finds some people who he considers are not wounded people -- "Interpreter: You can check and then if you find something you can --"

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you recognise the man wearing a helmet, the officer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that is General Pavkovic, Nebojsa Pavkovic of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This is the one you just mentioned was dispatched by the SSNO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. He may have been colonel at the time. I mean, he's -- but he ended as a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Let's continue playing.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "But what does he want? "Nicholas Borsinger: I want nothing. Tell. First of all I want nothing. I must comply with instructions I get of an agreement that the JNA has signed. That is all. I want nothing. "I have a responsibility and --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "So why isn't he talking to us? "Interpreter: Yes, go ahead. "You cannot go with the car. "Nicholas Borsinger: The Colonel tells me I cannot go. "Interpreter: You cannot go with the car you can go on your own.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "At the tail of the column there are your colleagues from the International Red Cross. "Interpreter: On the back of the -- there are your colleagues, our colleagues from International Red Cross. You know them?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Who are these people? "Interpreter: Colleagues from Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Do they work together or is he doing something separately? "Interpreter: With you or you -- "Nicholas Borsinger: Yes, they work together with me. "Interpreter: Why are you not with them? "Nicholas Borsinger: Because since I -- "Interpreter: Let him go and join them, be together with them. "Nicholas Borsinger: I meant to be ... according to this agreement I meant to be in the hospital since last night at 8.00.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "First of all, we don't have an agreement. Where is that agreement? Show me. "Nicholas Borsinger: How can I show the agreement which was signed by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Tell this gentleman that we should end this conversation. If he wants on his own responsibility to walk to the hospital, let him go ahead. But the JNA is not taking any responsibility for his security and safety. He can only go as part of the column and then I will guarantee his safety. "Nicholas Borsinger: But I must go in my car, I must go in my car. "Interpreter: So it means you have to go in the convoy.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Let him park the car, this vehicle must be moved to the left or to the right so the convoy can pass."

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, you have heard the part of the conversation when Nebojsa Pavkovic is saying there is no agreement or we don't have an agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: You heard that, yes. And with respect to what you told us earlier, your answer was that you would have expected the army leadership to convey this agreement down its chain of command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And just as a reminder, I mean we don't have to show the document, we could if we have to, but do you remember who signed the document on behalf of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it's -- I mean, I have it in my report, page 470, General Andrija Raseta, who was acting as a senior negotiator for the JNA at the time, and prior to that he -- I think he was a commander of the 5th Corps or part of the command of the 5th Corps located in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And -- yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, might I apply to tender this clip, please, 65 ter 5006?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Shall be assigned Exhibit P1693. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we've seen that the JNA signed the evacuation agreement on the 18th of November. We have now seen the video where Nebojsa Pavkovic is saying that there is no agreement. I would like you to look at 65 ter 669, please and that is at tab 191. Yes. Now, you refer to this document in your report and this is another one of those SSNO bulletins, so the 22nd of November 1991. I would like to go to the bottom of page 2 in the English version, please. And we can remain on the same page in the B/C/S version. Now, you see the first sentence here, this is two days after the date when the evacuation would have taken place in Vukovar. "The presence of European Community Observer Mission representatives did not help to evacuate children, women, and other civilians in Vukovar, desirous of moving to the territory of the Republic of Croatia. In spite of the signed agreement on the evacuation and the understanding that there would be no shooting during the evacuations." It carries on to say that: "Croatian armed forces deployed in the villages Nustar and Vinkovci fired on the front and rear lines of evacuees, convoys, whereupon the JNA unit in the presence of the ECMM diverted them to a safer area." Now, looking at this document what can you say with respect to the JNA's position with respect to the evacuation agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would just like to seek clarification whether you want to refer to the Zagreb Agreement for the hospital or other evacuation agreements?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: The Zagreb Agreement, yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding -- maybe I'm wrong, you know, but it's quite a while since I looked at the Zagreb Agreement, that it is confined to the hospital, whereas for the other evacuations there were other agreements. But again if you show me the agreement, then I can refresh my memory and I'm in a better position to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Absolutely. I believe I have the number here. It is P1461 at tab 174.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian, while we are waiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You are referring to the evacuation agreement as the Zagreb Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If I remember well, yesterday I think we were talking about the Raseta Agreement. Is -- are we talking about the same thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, we are. I believe in the report at 470 -- page 470, we are talking about the Zagreb Agreement and signed by Andrija Raseta, but perhaps Mr. Theunens can explain. But generally if I ask the questions the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you agree that the Zagreb Agreement -- what is called the Zagreb Agreement and the Raseta Agreement are one and the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, Your Honours. I wasn't familiar with the name "Raseta Agreement," but Andrija Raseta is the person who signed for the JNA --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- so probably that's why he's mentioned in the context of that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, the evacuation agreement is in front of you if you would like to take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, Your Honours, first paragraph talks about the following agreement regarding a convoy to evacuate the wounded and sick from the Vukovar Hospital. There were several evacuations. There were a few already prior to the evacuation of the hospital. I think there was already something in October to move injured people out from Vukovar as the city was under siege. There was the Mitnica evacuation, the members of the ZNG who surrendered in Mitnica I think on the 18th. We have the evacuation of the people from the hospital and then there were also -- there was also an evacuation -- I mean large-scale evacuation of civilians from Vukovar because it was decided -- I mean, it was obvious that these people could not reside in a city that was largely destroyed. And as can be seen from situation reports from mainly the 1st Military District covering the 20th of November to, let's say, the 23rd of November time-period, some of these convoys are not received or not allowed through by the Croatian authorities because of course the evacuation of mainly Croats from Vukovar would actually consolidate Serbian control over the city. And there is -- there are some problems, convoys are sent back and so on. But this is something else than the evacuation of the hospital and this is what I wanted to raise when Mr. Demirdjian asked his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. And under item 2 here do I understand that this is where the Republic of Croatia and the JNA undertake to guarantee a cease-fire so that there would be no shooting during the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during this evacuation indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can I return to that document which we were looking at which was 65 ter 669. And go to page 2 at the bottom again, please. Yes, so focusing again on that second sentence which says that in spite of the signed agreement on the evacuation and the understanding there would be no shooting, are you saying that you're not able to conclude as to which evacuation exactly this relates to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, yeah. I mean, for sure the Zagreb Agreement or the agreement on the evacuation of the hospital, is a signed agreement. I'm not sure for the other evacuations, whether there are any signed agreements. So that's why I would prefer not to draw a conclusion because I would have to check first whether for the other evacuations there were signed agreements.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. Can we move now to page 478 of your report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before we do that, is this the document we MFI'd a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: It is not, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But by all means this -- the translation problem, could you have it solved by the end of the week?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: This one I believe is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: No, the one we MFI'd because there was a translation problem, you know, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Just the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- the problem about the officers and the superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The word officer and superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I will ask that we do that -- I will ask Mr. Laugel to organise that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So by the end of the week?

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: In fact, if it's one word, I could even ask that this be done by the close of business today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. The sooner the better. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, in page 478 of your report which is page 538 in B/C/S, from this page onwards we see several orders and reports on the 20th of November. The first one that you were dealing with on this page - and I will wait for it to come on the screen - this is the 20th of November order number 439-1 issued by Mile Mrksic at 6.00 in the morning on settling the issues of daily activities. Now, we see the second sentence under item number 1 which says: "Simultaneously evacuate and transport civilians, the wounded, and the sick from the hospital in Vukovar." Now, have you seen any other orders with respect to the evacuation of the hospital in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. And actually, this document allows to clarify my earlier answer to the question where like I need to specify that I didn't see specific references to the Zagreb Agreement and the modalities like the presence of international observers and ECMM and so on in connection to the evacuation by the JNA of the hospital. But here obviously there is an order from OG South instructing subordinate units to evacuate people from Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, turning to doctrine again and the regulations in the JNA, how do you qualify an evacuation operation? How is that provided for?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- among SFRY armed forces doctrinal documents there is a regulation on -- for the military police on -- I think on the guarding of prisoners of war, and this is a document we -- I mean, I don't recall the exact name, but it's -- it was extensively discussed in the Vukovar case, which basically explains how prisoners of war should be guarded, how any movements of prisoners of war should be organised, which measures should be taken by whom, not just measures to prevent them from escaping but measures to protect them. And so we checked that document, for example, with at least one commander from the military police battalion of the Guards Motorised Brigade at the time of the events in Vukovar, and he told us at the time that this was an authentic document that was applicable then. So just in a nutshell there were indeed specific regulations available on how such an operation should be conducted not just from the security point of view but also logistical point of view and ensuring protection of all these prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And how do you view this order that we have in front of us here that has two lines basically with respect to the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of this order from Operational Group South, the one -- the subordinate who would be responsible for leading and conducting the evacuation operation would develop his own orders to his subordinates and at the end the section commander of the -- of a military police section of ten persons who would be involved in evacuation would know what to do, where, when, how, and would know how to respond in any situation that may occur during the implementation of the order. So orders at the higher level are, in general, more general. And I mean, the lower you go the more specific they become.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to look at a -- well, just for the record this document that we have on the screen is also 65 ter 652 at tab 186. I would like us to look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Before -- Mr. Demirdjian, before you go to another document, I would like to have something clarified by the witness. Mr. Theunens, the order is to evacuate civilians, the wounded and the sick from the hospital. How would you interpret this order or how do you suppose that the subordinates should interpret this order? I mean with regard to the people to be evacuated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seen in the context of other documents of OG South of that time-period, Your Honours, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I would rather like you to give first your opinion about what this would have meant to the people who read this order and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I mean, just looking at the text it would mean anyone who is a civilian, whatever situation they're in; then the wounded, whatever their origin would be, whether they would be civilian or military or maybe police; and sick also irrespective of their allegiance or -- I mean the group to which they would belong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's exactly what I wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And now when you put it in the context of other documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the context, the JNA -- I mean, OG South, and in particular the security organs are convinced that among the patients of Vukovar Hospital at that time there are members of the ZNG. There are also, and I think they are quoted in the amalgamated report, that in certain locations of the hospital there are "Ustashas" and that even prisoners, I mean members of the Guards Motorised Brigade who are held in detention by the ZNG are mistreated in the hospital. So in that context, of course, maybe one would have another interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Demirdjian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And the next document I would like us to have on the screen is 65 ter 639 at tab 182. This is a document which you quote at page 476 of your report. It is also at page 536 in the B/C/S version. Now, the first document you were quoting earlier was of the 20th of November at 6.00 in the morning. We're looking now at a document or we will look at it -- yes, at a document of the 20th of November at 1800 hours, so 12 hours after the first one we looked earlier. It is an OG South regular combat report to the 1st Military District and the SSNO. Actually, on that matter how do you interpret the fact that the document is sent both to the 1st MD and the SSNO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that in peace time the -- or in -- I mean the regular subordination of the Guards Motorised Brigade is to the SSNO, and by the order that was issued on the 30th of September the Guards Motorised Brigade was subordinated to the 1st Military District. So it's not unusual that the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade informs both his current superior, the 1st Military District, as well as his previous superior of the activities of his unit. And also I think this has to be seen in light of the importance of the operations around Vukovar and given the strategic importance of Vukovar according to senior JNA officers at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, scrolling down to item number 2 of this document, we see that OG South refers to orders given by the 1st Military District, tasks relating to the take-over of the hospital and the MUP building, et cetera. And if we go to the top of page 2 and in the B/C/S version we can stay on the same page, you should see a -- what looks like a second paragraph beginning with "during selection." "During selection, transport, and hand-over of prisoners of war everything was handled in accordance with the Geneva Conventions on prisoners of war. Measures were taken on strengthening the command and control, order, and discipline in the units." Now, with respect to the documents we have seen previously from the 1st Military District, do you know what is this reference to prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are references, Your Honours, in my report. There is a -- for example, an order signed by the Chief of Staff of the 1st Military District that there can be no exchanges of prisoners of war unless it has been agreed upon by the highest command levels. I will be able to find the exact reference of that order. So the JNA -- I mean, SFRY armed forces or in fact the JNA, they want to centralise the whole issue of exchanges of prisoners of war and that's also why, for example, senior officers of the security organs are sent to Vukovar before the evacuation of the hospital because these prisoners of war can be used, yeah, to exchange, it's one-for-one exchange, so they want to avoid that at the lower level subordinate commanders decide on their own -- by their own -- like, who is to be exchanged against whom. So they really want to keep this centralised, and an additional benefit of having centralised control is it's easier to ensure the enforcement or the application of Geneva and other relevant conventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, with respect to this sentence here, it doesn't specify who the prisoners of war were handed over to; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but in light of the previous order then it should be clear to any commander that since he is not allowed to hand them over, yeah, that the hand-over is only going to happen at a higher level, so it shouldn't be a concern of the subordinate commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Very well. On that note I want to show you a document of the same day from the 1st Military District, it's 65 ter 656, tab 187. Yes, thank you. Now, you see this is a document of the 1st Military District on the 20th of November and it is entitled "combat report ." I want to take you to page 4 in the English version and that is page 2 in the B/C/S version. Can we go -- can we scroll down a bit in the English version to look at the paragraph which starts with: "During the day OG South captured the hospital and the MUP building. Control was taken of the hospital building and the examination of the wounded and sick began in order to identify MUP and ZNG members who are hiding in the hospital among the wounded." So this goes back to what you were telling us a moment ago. Now, this order -- this report, I apologise, includes some detail that I was -- we didn't see in the report of the OG South. Are there any OG South documents which include this information about the examination of the wounded and the sick?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall -- I mean, I'm just looking at which wording is used in the OG South daily reports or any mention of wounded and sick. For example, there is footnote 1408 that is for the 21st of November, this is on page 481. I'm just looking at what I have for the 20th of November. But as I mention in my report, there are no specific entries in OG South documents or in the war diary referring specifically to the hospital evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, we have seen two OG South reports on the 20th of November. Does the JNA also use other means of reporting than written reports?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, there can always be oral reporting, but again -- and I think maybe -- probably I mention in the report, given the importance of the event and the presence of international observers and the interest shown by the SSNO, I mean the security administration, the 1st Military District, to the overall handling of the end of hostilities and the evacuation of civilians, it would make sense to have written -- I mean to have -- to code in written reporting because written report is actually the report, yeah, that is being sent on a regular basis and you would expect that it covers all activities, so why would you not include an important event as the evacuation of the hospital? It would be unusual or it is unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Now, you come to that conclusion at page 480 of your report. If we could display 65 ter 556, please. At page 480 of your report you discuss the fact that there is an entry in the war diary of the 80th Motorised Brigade, and I'll conclude on this topic, so this -- 65 ter 556, tab 155 of the lists, very well. And could we go to page 16 in the English version and that's page 15 in the B/C/S version. If we scroll down to the bottom of the page in the English version and zoom in to the entry at around 4 -- 1600 hours. Yes. And same thing for the B/C/S version. Thank you. We see the entry here which says that: "The brigade commander" at 4.00 in the afternoon "requests that the detachment commander relieve officers from guarding the captured ZNG and MUP members, the cVP and brigade command were engaged for this." Can you tell us what is the cVP, if I'm pronouncing it right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's the Ceta and Vojna policija, it's the military police platoon if I'm not mistaken. VP stands for military police. I think that Ceta is a platoon if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And the next entry at 10.35 -- 2235 hours: "The security for the camp for captured ZNG" and let's move to the next page in the English version on the top part, yeah, "so the security for the camp for captured ZNG and MUP members was withdrawn from the Ovcara sector and they were replaced by the Vukovar territorials. The detachment of the military police and duty organs from the brigade command returned to Negoslavci village and the command post." Now, what do you make out of these two entries, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think the language is clear. It means that 80th -- commander of the 80th Brigade must have been ordered to take the measures he has taken, i.e., withdraw his personnel from Ovcara. We know from other documents that the 80th Brigade had a presence in Ovcara area and that the 80th Brigade was subordinated to OG South at the time of the events, even afterwards. Just hypothetically, if the commander of the 80th Brigade had issued these orders without the approval or the authorisation or the orders from the commander of OG South, the commander of OG South would afterwards have held the commander of the 80th Brigade accountable for failure to implement his orders or for doing things that were not in accordance with his orders, and I haven't seen any such response from the commander of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: And I know that we're passing the time but if I may give one last question to close this chapter, Your Honours. Here it says that the -- on the previous page the security for the camp were withdrawn from Ovcara and were replaced by Vukovar territorials. Is that what it says? And Vukovar territorials refers to what exactly?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again in the context of other documents, it refers to members of the local Serb TO in Vukovar, including volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: I think it's time to adjourn, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Indeed. Mr. Theunens, this is the end of the second day of your testimony. You're not released, which again means don't discuss your testimony with anybody, don't talk to any of the parties. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: See you tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could we discuss tomorrow morning at the beginning of the hearing the plan -- the further planning of this witness, the end of examination-in-chief to start of cross-examination, the timing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DEMIRDJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
